items.title: Generally Available: Azure Front Door Premium now supports Azure Private Link origins in UAE North
items.description:
You can now set UAE North as a region for Azure Private Link-enabled origins in your Azure Front Door Premium profile. Azure Private Link-enabled origins in Azure Front Door allow you to deliver content to your end-users through public Azure Front Door endpoints while ensuring that your origins remain inaccessible to the public internet. 
Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available:  Azure Databricks Supervisor Agent
items.description:
Introducing Supervisor Agent, now Generally Available in Azure Databricks. Supervisor Agent is part of the Azure Databricks Agent Bricks Platform. Supervisor Agent brings a breakthrough in agentic intelligence—using a dynamic supervisor pattern that understands your desired outcome and orchestrates the optimal path in real time.

With Supervisor Agent, organizations can finally unify fragmented, single‑purpose agents into a cohesive, high‑performance team. Each workflow becomes smarter, faster, and more reliable—fully governed and secured through Unity Catalog. 

Built for scale and engineered for production, Supervisor Agent unlocks a new era of enterprise‑grade agentic automation on Azure Databricks.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Application Gateway for Containers - AKS managed add-on
items.description:
We're announcing public preview of an AKS managed add-on that simplifies the deployment and lifecycle management of Application Gateway for Containers and its ALB Controller. With the managed AKS add-on, you can enable Application Gateway for Containers with a single command for new or existing AKS clusters through Azure CLI, ARM, and Bicep. 

The managed add-on helps streamline operations by providing: 

  • Managed installation and updates of the ALB Controller (so you don't need to maintain Helm charts) 

  • Secure integration via managed identity with least-privilege permissions 

  • Simplified networking when using AKS managed virtual network configuration 

The add-on also integrates with AKS' managed Gateway API add-on for seamless management of Gateway API CRDs within your AKS cluster. 

Learn more: 

  • Deploy Application Gateway for Containers + AKS Add-on  

  • Application Gateway for Containers overview

items.title: Private Preview: Vaulted Backups for Azure Disk
items.description:
Today, Azure Disk Backup protects data by taking regular, crash-consistent snapshots of Azure Disks. These snapshots are stored within your subscription and tenant in a resource group, referred to as the Operational Tier in Azure Backup. This enables fast, operational recovery for scenarios such as accidental deletion or data corruption and is commonly used alongside Azure VM Backup, which provides application-aware protection for virtual machines.  

Backup best practices recommend a 3-2-1 strategy, including storing a copy of backups offsite in an isolated location securing against a tenant-level compromise. 

With the introduction of Vault Tier backups, Azure Disk Backup now complements Azure VM Backup by extending disk-level protection with vault-based isolation, independent access controls, and immutability. This enables recovery of trusted data during ransomware attacks or tenant compromises, bringing disk backups in line with Azure VM Backup grade cyber-recovery security.  

As part of this Private Preview, Azure Disk Backup introduces two key capabilities: 

  • Vault Tier Backup: Protect disk backups in a vault (offsite) to meet cyber-recovery, ransomware resilience, and compliance requirements. 

  • Regional Disaster Recovery: Restore disk backups to a paired Azure region, enabling new disaster-recovery scenarios alongside Azure VM Backup and Azure Site Recovery. 

If you’re interested in participating, sign up for the Private Preview here.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Monitor pipeline transformations
items.description:
Azure Monitor pipeline transformations feature is now Public Preview! This feature enables users to shape telemetry before it’s ingested into Azure Monitor, helping them control ingestion costs, improve data quality, and simplify analytics at scale.

Built into the Azure Monitor pipeline for edge and multi-cloud environments, transformations allow data types such as Syslog and CEF to be filtered, aggregated, standardized, and reshaped prior to ingestion. Automatic schema standardization and built-in validation guardrails ensure continued compatibility with standard tables, allowing users to apply transformations confidently without disrupting dataflow.

Transformations also include prebuilt KQL templates for common scenarios, along with advanced filtering and aggregation to reduce noise, lower ingestion volume, and summarize high frequency data into meaningful time windows. By shaping data closer to the source, Azure Monitor pipeline transformations deliver cleaner data and faster insights for high volume and complex telemetry environments. 

Learn more:

  • Configure Azure Monitor pipeline transformations 
  • Azure Monitor pipeline transformations demo

items.title: Private Preview: New planned datacenter region in Thailand (Thailand South)
items.description:
Microsoft is announcing our intent to establish a new datacenter region in Thailand. The datacenter region will expand the availability of Microsoft’s hyperscale cloud services in the region, facilitating enterprise-grade reliability, performance, and compliance with data residency and privacy standards.

Learn more.

items.title: ​Generally Available: Claude Opus 4.6 now available on Azure Databricks
items.description:
Azure Databricks now supports Anthropic Claude Opus 4.6 through Mosaic AI Model serving. Claude Opus 4.6 is Anthropic's most advanced model, delivering state-of-the-art performance on agentic coding, complex reasoning, and knowledge work tasks. The model features enhanced coding capabilities with improved planning, code review, and debugging skills, enabling it to operate reliably in large codebases and sustain long-running agentic workflows. 

Claude Opus 4.6 is ideal for developers building AI agents, enterprises requiring advanced code assistance, and teams working with complex analytical and research workflows. The model now runs securely within the Azure Databricks environment and is accessible through both pay-per-token and provisioned throughput options.


Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: AMD v6 confidential VMs in new regions for January 2026
items.description:
DCa/ECa v6 series AMD based confidential virtual machines are now generally available in 11 new regions: Canada Central, Canada East, Norway East, Norway West, Italy North, Germany North, France South, Australia East, West US, West US 3, Germany West Central.

This is in addition to the 6 regions announced during launch of these VMs: Korea Central, South Africa North, Switzerland North, UAE North, UK South, West Central US.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure virtual network routing appliance
items.description:
Azure Virtual Network routing appliance offers private connectivity for workloads across virtual networks. Using specialized hardware, it delivers low latency and high throughput, and optimal performance compared to virtual machines.   

Deployed into private subnet, where it acts as a managed forwarding router. Traffic can be routed using User Defined Routes (UDR) enabling spoke to spoke communication in traditional Hub & Spoke topologies.  

Configured as Azure resource, integrates seamlessly with Azure’s management and governance model. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Claude Opus 4.6, Available on Microsoft Foundry
items.description:
Claude Opus 4.6 is now available in Microsoft Foundry, bringing Anthropic’s most advanced reasoning model to a secure, enterprise-ready platform built on Azure. With support for complex coding, knowledge work, and agent-driven workflows, including long-context reasoning and governed computer use, customers can move faster from experimentation to production while maintaining trust, security, and operational rigor. This release enables organizations to deploy frontier AI for real-world, high‑stakes scenarios across development, analysis, and automation.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure NetApp Files Elastic zone-redundant service level
items.description:
Azure NetApp Files Elastic zone-redundant storage (ANF Elastic ZRS) is an advanced high-availability service level for Azure NetApp Files that provides continuous data access with zero data loss, even if an entire Azure Availability Zone goes offline. Built on Azure’s Zone-redundant storage (ZRS) architecture and compute infrastructure, ANF Elastic ZRS synchronously replicates file data across availability zones within one region. By eliminating single points of failure, it ensures mission-critical workloads remain online and protected without requiring special configuration or manual intervention. This makes it ideal for applications that demand uncompromising resilience and in-region data protection. 

Azure NetApp Files Elastic ZRS provides consistent performance for metadata-heavy workloads across VMs and containers, making it well suited for AI, analytics, and Kubernetes/OpenShift environments. Whether you’re running mission critical workloads, AKS and containerized apps, cloud‑native applications, or general file shares, Azure NetApp Files Elastic ZRS delivers continuity without compromise, cost‑effective scalability, and operational simplicity. You can create volumes as small as 1 GiB, giving you the flexibility to optimize storage for workloads of any size. 

This new service is in Preview in these regions and we will be rapidly expanding.

Learn more: 

  • Understand Elastic zone-redundant storage service level
  • Create a NetApp Elastic account in Azure NetApp Files

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Kubernetes Fleet Manager namespace-scoped resource placement
items.description:
Namespace-scoped resource placement, now in preview for Azure Kubernetes Fleet Manager, delivers fine‑grained control over selection and propagation of individual namespace‑scoped resources across multiple clusters.  

 

This new capability means it is now possible to use Fleet Manager’s intelligent placement where a single namespace hosts multiple applications with different lifecycles and distribution requirements, or where teams using managed fleet namespaces need per‑workload scheduling based on specific cluster properties or capacity. 

 

Those that are using Fleet Manager’s existing cluster-scoped resource placement will find familiar constructs including placement policies and staged rollouts, making it a simple step to start using namespace-scoped resource placement. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Container Storage v2.1.0 now with Elastic SAN integration and on demand installation
items.description:
Azure Container Storage v2.1.0 is now generally available. This release adds native Elastic SAN support and introduces a lightweight, on-demand installation model to simplify deployment and operations for Kubernetes workloads on Azure. 

Elastic SAN Storage Type Support

With full support for Elastic SAN as a native storage type, you can provision scalable volume groups and consolidate large number of Kubernetes volumes under a single SAN resource, enabling faster attach and detach operations, higher throughput, and reduced management overhead for stateful workloads. The release also includes streamlined setup, improved defaults, and enhanced automation for Elastic SAN creation and volume group configuration.

On demand, modular Installation

Azure Container Storage v2.1.0 now supports modular, on-demand installation, allowing you to deploy only the components required for your selected storage type. This reduces cluster footprint, accelerates deployment, and simplifies lifecycle management.


Node Selector Support for component placement

Additionally, node selectors support enables precise control over where Azure Container Storage components run, helping optimize performance and resource usage in clusters with dedicated storage node pools or mixed topologies.
 
Learn more

items.title: Public Preview: X-Forwarded-For (XFF) grouping for rate limiting on Application Gateway WAF v2
items.description:
Application Gateway Web Application Firewall (WAF) v2 now supports additional rate‑limiting GroupBy options based on the X‑Forwarded‑For (XFF) HTTP header. This enables customers running Application Gateway behind proxies or CDNs to apply rate limits using the original client IP rather than the TCP source IP. In this preview, rate‑limiting rules can be grouped by Client Address (XFF) or Geo Location (XFF), helping security teams more accurately mitigate abusive or high‑volume traffic patterns without unintentionally throttling legitimate users. The capability integrates with existing Application Gateway WAF v2 custom rate‑limit rules and policies. 
Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Serverless workspaces in Azure Databricks
items.description:
Serverless workspaces in Azure Databricks are now generally available, offering a fully managed workspace type that comes preconfigured with serverless compute and default storage. They deliver an enterprise-ready SaaS experience with zero infrastructure setup. With this release, customers can create Azure Databricks "Serverless" workspaces directly from the Azure portal to run production workloads in minutes, rapidly spin up short-lived environments for training and testing, and empower admins who lack direct cloud provisioning permissions to deploy and manage secure, governed Azure Databricks environments at scale, all natively available to every user in your Entra tenant.

Learn more.

items.title: Retirement: Azure Front Door and Azure CDN profiles will end support for DHE cipher suites on April 1, 2026
items.description:
As part of our ongoing commitment to security, Azure Front Door (Standard, Premium, Classic) and Azure CDN from Microsoft (Classic) services will no longer support  weak cipher suites TLS_DHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 and TLS_DHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 on April 1 2026 for both ‘client to service’ connections and ‘service to origin’ connections.

Required action

To ensure uninterrupted service and maintain strong encryption standards, take the following actions:

  1. Update your origins to disable DHE ciphers and use any of the recommended cipher suites. Follow our documentation to see how to update cipher suites for some of the common origin types used with Azure Front Door/Azure CDN.
  2. Inform your clients to only use the recommended ciphers while connecting to your domains hosted on Azure Front Door/Azure CDN. If you own any of the clients, update them to use the recommended ciphers.
  3. For Front Door Standard/Premium profiles, you can also use the Configure Azure Front Door TLS policy feature to disable the DHE ciphers in advance before 1 April 2026. For all Front Door (Standard, Premium, Classic) and Azure CDN from Microsoft (Classic) profiles, we will disable the DHE ciphers after April 1 2026.

Help and support

For more information and guidance regarding DHE cipher retire, refer to our documentation.

If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A. If you have a support plan and need technical help, please submit a support request .

items.title: Generally Available: Default Ruleset 2.2 in WAF for Azure Application Gateway
items.description:
Announcing the general availability of Default Rule Set (DRS) 2.2 for Web Application Firewall on Azure Application Gateway.

The Azure-managed DRS provides active protection against common web vulnerabilities and exploits. It also includes Microsoft Threat Intelligence collection rules, authored in collaboration with our intelligence teams, to deliver broader coverage, targeted vulnerability mitigations, and continual improvements in false-positive reduction.

DRS 2.2 is based on OWASP Core Rule Set 3.3.4, bringing refinements to existing detections and new protections, including rules that detect content types declared outside the actual content-type header and enhanced remote code execution (RCE) detections. An additional eight Microsoft Threat Intelligence rules expand coverage across SQL injection, XSS, and application-security attack patterns.

To significantly reduce legitimate traffic being blocked, DRS 2.2 ships at Paranoia Level (PL) 1 by default. PL1 includes high-signal, lower-noise rules that rarely trigger false positives. PL2 rules are disabled by default because they are more aggressive and typically require fine-tuning. You can keep PL2 disabled or selectively enable individual PL2 rules where warranted. 

Learn more.

items.title: Retirement: "Send data to Event Hubs & Storage (Preview)" retiring July 31, 2026
items.description:
On July 31, 2026, we'll retire preview feature “Send virtual machine client data to Event Hubs and Storage (Preview)” and it'll no longer be supported by Microsoft. You will not be able to create any new data collection rules using this feature, and any existing configurations using this capability will stop sending data. You will need to switch to alternatives described here to continue using AMA or other Azure solutions that provide more reliable, scalable and performant solutions to send data to respective destinations.

Note: The Azure Monitor agent (AMA) itself continues to be generally available and supported, without any impact from the retirement of this specific preview feature.

items.title: Retirement: Support for Python 3.10 ends on October 1, 2026 – upgrade your Azure Functions apps to Python 3.13
items.description:
In alignment with the end of community support, on October 1, 2026, support for Python 3.10 in Azure Functions will end. Your apps that are hosted on Functions will continue to run, but security updates and performance optimizations will no longer be available and we'll no longer provide customer service for Python 3.10. Learn more about Azure Functions stack version support. 

Required action 

To avoid potential security vulnerabilities and take advantage of the latest features, follow the steps to upgrade your Functions apps to Python 3.13 by 1 October 2026. 

Help and support 

If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A. If you have a support plan and you need technical help, open the Azure portal and select the question mark icon at the top of the page.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure AMD Turin Dasv7, Easv7, and Fasv7-series Virtual Machines
items.description:
The general purpose Dasv7 and Dalsv7, memory-optimized Easv7, and compute-optimized Fasv7, Falsv7, Famsv7 VMs, are now generally available with and without local disk support. These VMs are available in the following Azure regions: Australia East, Central US, Germany West Central, Japan East, North Europe, South Central US, Southeast Asia, UK South, West Europe, West US 2, and West US 3. The large 160 vCPU Easv7-series and Eadsv7-series sizes are available in North Europe, South Central US, West Europe, and West US 2. More regions are coming in 2026.

These virtual machines deliver significant enhancements over the previous generation, offering improved CPU performance, greater scalability, and expanded configuration options to meet the demands of a wide range of workloads. Key improvements include:  

  • Up to 35% CPU performance improvement compared to similarly sized v6 VMs 

  • Significant performance gains on other workloads:   

    • Up to 25% for Java-based workloads 

    • Up to 65% for in-memory cache applications 

    • Up to 80% for crypto workloads 

    • Up to 130% for web server applications   

  • New VM series introduced: Fadsv7, Faldsv7, and Famdsv7 with local disk support. 

These enhancements make the AMD v7-series VMs a compelling choice for customers seeking high performance, cost efficiency, and workload flexibility on Azure. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Databricks Agent Bricks Knowledge Assistant
items.description:
Azure Databricks Agent Bricks knowledge assistant empowers you to create, deploy, and manage AI agents directly within the Azure Databricks platform, using unified data and AI capabilities. This feature simplifies agent development by providing prebuilt components, secure integration with enterprise data, and scalable orchestration. With Agent Bricks, you can accelerate automation, enhance decision-making, and deliver personalized experiences all while maintaining compliance and governance standards under the Azure ecosystem. By combining the flexibility of open-source frameworks with the enterprise-grade security and reliability of Azure, Agent Bricks makes it easier for you to build high-quality, production-ready AI agents at scale with Azure Databricks. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Latest PostgreSQL minor versions supported by Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server
items.description:
PostgreSQL minor versions 18.1, 17.7, 16.11, 15.15, 14.20, and 13.23 are now supported by Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server.    

These minor version upgrades are automatically performed as part of the monthly planned maintenance in Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server. This upgrade automation ensures that your databases are always running the latest optimized versions without requiring manual intervention.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: 7th generation Intel-based VMs – Dlsv7/Dsv7/Esv7
items.description:
Announcing the preview of new Azure Dlsv7/Dsv7 General Purpose and Esv7 Memory Optimized Virtual Machines (VMs) powered by the latest Intel® Xeon® 6 processors (Granite Rapids). 

The latest Azure Intel-based v7 VMs are designed to power ever increasing compute demands in today’s data center environment and deliver exceptional performance across a wide range of workloads, from traditional enterprise applications to cutting edge AI.  

These VMs deliver several important features and improvements compared previous generation (v6) Intel-based VMs including: 

  • Up to 15% better general compute performance, powered by Intel® Xeon® 6 CPUs with turbo frequencies up to 4.2 GHz and up to 2x higher memory bandwidth 

  • Expanded sizes and memory capacity: Dsv7 and Esv7 VMs now scale up to 372 vCPUs with Esv7 VMs enabling up to 2.8TiB of memory 

  • Increased networking and remote storage performance driven by latest Azure Boost capabilities: 

    • Up to 400 Gbps networking bandwidth with the largest size 

    • Up to 800k IOPS and 20 GBps throughput to Premium v2 and Ultra Disk remote storage with the largest size 

Join the Preview 

Dlsv7, Dsv7, and Esv7 VM sizes with and without local NVMe temp disks will be available to test in preview in the East US 2 region. To request access to the preview, please fill out the survey form here. We look forward to hearing from you.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure NetApp Files support in OpenShift Virtualization
items.description:
Azure NetApp Files now enables fast virtual machine (VM) provisioning, instant cloning, and live migration in OpenShift Virtualization. It offers seamlessly scalable storage with predictable performance and enterprise data management for VM workloads from infrastructure VMs to business-critical databases. Support for Azure NetApp Files in OpenShift Virtualization is now in preview and is available in all Azure regions where Azure NetApp Files and Azure Red Hat OpenShift are offered. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Command Launcher for Java
items.description:
At Microsoft Ignite 2025, we announced the Public Preview of the Azure Command Launcher for Java, a new JVM launcher optimized specifically for Azure. This tool provides better default ergonomics for Java applications running in containers and virtual machines, ensuring more efficient use of resources right from the start. 

By using Azure Command Launcher for Java to automatically set JVM parameters tailored for cloud deployments, your workloads have reduced wasted memory and CPU cycles, improving first-deploy performance, and enhancing cost efficiency. This is ideal for developers, Ops, and SREs, who want better JVM defaults without diving deep into JVM tuning guides, and  develop and deploy cloud-native microservices.   

    

Key Features

  1. Automatically benefits from battle-tested defaults for cloud-native and container workloads.   

  2. Optimizes resource utilization by setting JVM parameters tailored for cloud deployments.   

  3. Improves likelihood of first-deploy performance and cost efficiency.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Deployment safeguards – pod security standard support in AKS
items.description:
Organizations deploying workloads on Kubernetes often need a consistent way to enforce pod security configurations across clusters. Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) now supports Pod Security Standards within Deployment Safeguards, enabling centralized management of Baseline, Restricted, and Privileged standards at scale. This capability allows teams to ensure that deployment manifests comply with selected security standards, help technical practitioners strengthen workload security, reduce configuration drift, and simplify the rollout of cluster-wide security controls. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: StandardV2 NAT Gateway with zone-redundancy and StandardV2 public IPs
items.description:
StandardV2 SKU NAT Gateway is now generally available, delivering enhanced resiliency, greater performance, and dual-stack connectivity, all at the same price as the Standard SKU.  


StandardV2 Public IP addresses and prefixes are also generally available. 


StandardV2 NAT Gateway requires StandardV2 public IPs; Standard SKU public IPs are not supported.  

What’s new with StandardV2 NAT Gateway:  

  • Zone-redundancy: Automatically maintains outbound connectivity during single zone failures in availability zone-enabled regions.  

  • Enhanced performance: Up to 100 Gbps of throughput and 10 million packets per second—double the Standard SKU capacity.  

  • Dual-stack support: Attach up to 16 IPv6 and 16 IPv4 public IP addresses for future ready connectivity.  

  • Traffic insights with flow logs: Gain detailed IP-level visibility of traffic for troubleshooting and compliance verification.  

Pricing and availability  

  • StandardV2 NAT Gateway is the same price as the Standard SKU.  

  • Available in most public cloud regions, rollout planned for remaining regions in 2026. Learn more about remaining unsupported regions.  

  • Deploy through Portal, CLI, Powershell, Bicep, and ARM. Terraform support coming soon.  

Learn more:  

  • StandardV2 NAT Gateway   

  • StandardV2 NAT Gateway flow logs  

  • StandardV2 public IPs

items.title: Generally Available: Reporting in Playwright Workspaces (part of Azure App Testing)
items.description:
Reporting capabilities are now live in Playwright Workspaces. The latest update brings you an integrated, flexible and collaborative reporting experience designed to make debugging tests in Playwright Workspaces easier, faster and more efficient. Customers can bring their own Azure storage accounts to store and govern their test artifacts. Playwright Workspaces is a fully managed service for end-to-end web testing, built on top of Playwright. With Playwright Workspaces, you can significantly speed up test execution by running tests in parallel using managed cloud-based browsers. 
Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Application volume group for Oracle create data protection volume group (API)
items.description:
The functionality of application volume group for Oracle has been expanded with the ability to create data protection volumes in a volume group with the same anti-affinity layout as production volume groups. 

Customers benefit from this ability for creating disaster recovery volume layouts that support production failover to a zone or region of their choice. 

 

This feature is available in all regions that support Azure NetApp Files.  

 

Learn more: 

  • What's new in Azure NetApp Files 

  • Understand Azure NetApp Files application volume group for Oracle

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Load Testing in Switzerland North
items.description:
Azure Load Testing capability in Azure App Testing is now generally available in Switzerland North. Customers can now use Azure Load Testing, a fully managed load-testing service to generate high scale load and run simulations, easily identify performance bottlenecks through a rich dashboard of client-side and server-side metrics, get AI powered actionable insights, and integrate load tests into their CI/CD workflows. Customers can get started without any knowledge of load-testing tools, or use their existing Apache JMeter or Locust scripts.

Learn more:
  • about Azure Load Testing.
  • go to feedback forum.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure File Sync in Israel Central
items.description:
Azure File Sync enables seamless tiering of data from on-premises Windows Servers to Azure Files for hybrid use cases and simplified migration. It also enables you to leverage the performance, flexibility and compatibility of your on-premises File Server while leveraging the scale and cost effectiveness of Azure Files.

The expansion into Israel Central brings the service closer to organizations in these regions, offering lower latency, better performance, and support for local data residency requirements.

If Azure File Sync is not yet available in your preferred region, please fill out this survey to express interest.  
Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Ubuntu 24.04 support in AKS
items.description:
Customers upgrading AKS clusters often need a clear and flexible path to adopt new OS versions without disrupting workloads. Ubuntu 24.04 is now generally available on AKS starting with Kubernetes version 1.32, with containerd 2.0 enabled by default.  

It can be enabled using the new Ubuntu2404 OS SKU in Kubernetes 1.32 and above, or by using the standard Ubuntu OS SKU in Kubernetes 1.35 and above, where Ubuntu 24.04 becomes the default.  

Existing clusters already using the Ubuntu OS SKU will automatically migrate to Ubuntu 24.04 when upgraded to Kubernetes 1.35 or later.  

For rollback or testing scenarios, AKS also now supports the Ubuntu2204 OS SKU across Kubernetes versions 1.25 through 1.36, allowing practitioners to switch OS versions without requiring a Kubernetes version change. These options provide more control over OS lifecycle management and simplify migration planning for cluster operators. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: User delegation SAS for Azure Tables, Azure Files, and Azure Queues
items.description:
User delegation SAS for Azure Tables, Azure Files, and Azure Queues is now available in public preview. User delegation (UDK) SAS is already generally available for blobs, and this release extends that support to tables, files, and queues.


User delegation SAS allows users to create a more secure SAS token than account or service SAS by tying the SAS token to the delegator. This extension of UDK SAS will allow users to set SAS tokens at the table, table entity, queue, queue entity, file container, and individual file level. Any SAS token set at the higher level will provide access to all table/queue/file entities within, and any SAS token set at the base level will only provide access to that individual entity.

 

There is no additional cost to use user delegation SAS. Pricing is based on the standard read/write transaction costs for your storage account type. To learn more, please see Azure Storage Pricing.

 

This preview is available in all public regions.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Ubuntu 24.04 support in AKS
items.description:
Ubuntu 24.04 is now generally available on AKS in Kubernetes version 1.32 and above. Containerd 2.0 is enabled by default. Ubuntu 24.04 is default with `Ubuntu` OS Sku in kubernetes version 1.35 and above. 

There are two ways that Ubuntu 24.04 can be enabled. 

In Kubernetes version 1.32 and above, you can use the ‘Ubuntu2404’ OS Sku. This OS Sku can help you migrate existing clusters before you reach the minimum kubernetes version for Ubuntu 24.04 as default on AKS. 

In Kubernetes version 1.35 and above, you can use ‘Ubuntu’ OS Sku which defaults to Ubuntu 24.04. If you are already using `Ubuntu` OS Sku and upgrade to kubernetes version 1.35 or above, you’ll automatically migrate to Ubuntu 24.04. 

While migrating to Ubuntu 24.04, you can rollback to Ubuntu 22.04 by using the new OS SKU “Ubuntu2204” in Kubernetes versions 1.25 to 1.36. This functionality allows for more flexibility in testing and upgrading your OS versions without requiring a Kubernetes version upgrade.    

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Cosmos DB Mirroring with Private Endpoints
items.description:
Available now in Public Preview, you can configure Azure Cosmos DB accounts with virtual networks or private endpoints to work with Microsoft Fabric mirroring. This feature allows you to preserve your enhanced network security and seamlessly replicate your operational data in Cosmos DB using Mirroring into your Fabric Workspaces. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Geo-Replication for Azure Service Bus Premium
items.description:
The Geo-Replication feature for Azure Service Bus in the premium tier is now generally available. The Service Bus Geo-Replication feature is one of the options to insulate Azure Service Bus applications against outages and disasters, providing replication of both metadata (entities, configuration, properties) and data (message data and message property / state changes).  

The Geo-Replication feature ensures that the metadata and data of a namespace are continuously replicated from a primary region to one or more secondary regions. Moreover, it allows promoting any secondary region to primary, at any time.   

Promoting a secondary repoints the endpoint for the namespace to the selected secondary region and switches the roles between the primary and secondary region. The promotion is nearly instantaneous once initiated and doesn’t require any changes on the client side.  

More information on this feature can be found in the documentation.

items.title: Generally Available: Cloud-native apps on Kubernetes pricing calculator scenario
items.description:
The new cloud-native apps on Kubernetes pricing calculator scenario allows teams to estimate the total cost of ownership for a production-ready AKS cluster with other key Azure services, including Azure Container Registry, Azure Monitoring, Microsoft Defender for Cloud, and more. The calculator scenario provides an architecture diagram and cost estimate with customizable inputs to fit your workload requirements. Whether you are migrating legacy workloads or deploying new applications, including microservices, web apps, AI, GPU workloads, and databases, this calculator scenario will help you establish your cost baseline. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Premium SSD v2 Disk is now available in Austria East and in a second Availability Zone in Japan West
items.description:
Azure Premium SSD v2 is now available in Austria East and in a second Availability Zone in Japan West.  

Azure Premium SSD v2, a next-generation general-purpose block storage solution, offers sub-millisecond latencies and exceptional price performance for IO-intensive workloads at a low cost. Premium SSD v2 is suited for a broad range of enterprise production scenarios, including SQL Server, Oracle, MariaDB, SAP, Cassandra, MongoDB, big data/analytics, and gaming on virtual machines or stateful containers.   

If Premium SSD v2 is unavailable in your preferred region and you would like to use it, please complete this survey.   

Learn more:   

  • Read the documentation.  

  • For more information about Premium SSD v2 Disk Storage pricing, visit the Azure Managed Disks pricing page.

items.title: Retirement: Deprecation of Custom Resource Providers
items.description:
In 2026, Azure Resource Manager will be deprecating the Custom Resource Provider (CuRP) service.

We will retire the feature by October 31, 2026. We will be performing a scream test on October 27, 2025, as part of this deprecation. On July 31, 2026, creates, updates, patches, and actions to custom resources and resource providers will be blocked. You will only be able to read and delete your custom resources and resource providers.

We understand that this deprecation may be an inconvenience to you and your team. Here are some potential CuRP alternatives you can use to support your existing workflows.

If your CuRP scenario:

  • Only involves triggering an endpoint without the need for persistent resource management, consider Deployment Scripts.
  • Only involves triggering an endpoint without the need for persistent resource management, and you use Bicep, consider Bicep Extensions.
  • Involves triggering several different endpoints or services for your solution, consider Azure Functions.

If you have any questions, please ask your Microsoft account manager to email curpdeprecation@microsoft.com with your name, company name, email contact, and subscription ID.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Blob-to-Blob migration made simple with Azure Storage Mover
items.description:
Azure Storage Mover’s new Azure Blob container-to-container migration feature is now in Public Preview, empowering organizations to move data between two Blob containers within the same or different storage accounts, subscriptions or Azure regions securely, reliably, and at scale. With this release, customers can eliminate manual pipelines and tools, automate migrations in the Azure portal, and gain real-time visibility into every job. 

Key benefits: 

1. Fully Managed and Scalable 

Azure Storage Mover is a fully managed service, meaning Microsoft handles the infrastructure, scaling, and reliability. This reduces operational overhead and ensures consistent performance across large-scale transfers. 

2. No Agent Required 

Unlike on-premises migrations, cloud-to-cloud transfers do not require deploying an agent. This simplifies setup and reduces the need for additional compute resources. 

3. High-Speed, Parallel Transfers 

Storage Mover supports parallel file transfers, enabling faster migration of large datasets. This is particularly useful when moving data across regions or between storage accounts with high throughput requirements. 

Get started today and simplify your cloud data estate with Azure Storage Mover’s Blob-to-Blob migration. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Service Bus SDK type bindings in Azure Functions for Node.js
items.description:
Azure Functions triggers and bindings enable you to easily integrate event and data sources with function applications.  

 

Now that SDK type bindings support for Azure Blob Storage is available, we’re also introducing support for Service Bus SDK type bindings in your Node.js function apps.  

 

This means in JavaScript or TypeScript function apps you can now interact with a ServiceBusMessageContext type offering advanced messaging functionality.  


Learn more:

  • SDK type bindings for Service Bus in JavaScript and TypeScript 
  • SDK type bindings for Service Bus in JavaScript and TypeScript samples

items.title: Public Preview: Use Azure SRE Agent with Azure Cosmos DB
items.description:
You can now simplify how you diagnose and resolve issues in your applications running on Azure Cosmos DB with the introduction of the Azure Cosmos DB Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) Agent, built on the Azure SRE Agent platform. This new capability gives you deeper visibility into the health and performance of your database workloads by combining client-side telemetry with server-side diagnostics, allowing you to identify problems faster and understand them more clearly. 

 

Using the Azure Cosmos DB SRE Agent, you receive recommendations that help you improve performance, strengthen security, and optimize cost. Instead of only detecting issues, the agent guides you through best practices tailored to your workload. You can use it to understand why throttling may be occurring, how configuration choices impact performance or reliability, or whether your application is encountering hidden connectivity challenges. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Avaailable: Azure SQL updates for early December 2025
items.description:
In mid-December 2025, the following updates and enhancements were made to Azure SQL:  

  • Identify causes that auto-resume serverless workloads using Activity Log in Azure SQL Database to troubleshoot and optimize access patterns. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure NetApp Files advanced ransomware protection
items.description:
Azure NetApp Files advanced ransomware protection (ANF ARP) is now in Public Preview.  ANF ARP is designed to help organizations proactively detect, respond to, and recover from ransomware threats on cloud volumes. ANF ARP monitors Azure NetApp Files volumes for suspicious activity using file extension profiling, entropy, and IOPS patterns. When a threat is detected, the system creates a point-in-time snapshot, enabling rapid evaluation and recovery. Notifications are sent via Azure Activity log and attack reports are retained for 30 days. There is no specific additional charge for ANF ARP but see Considerations section when sizing your deployment to accommodate ANF ARP. 

Azure NetApp Files advanced ransomware protection is now Public Preview in all regions.

Learn more:  

  • What's new in Azure NetApp Files  

  • Configure Azure NetApp Files advanced ransomware protection

items.title: Generally Available: Azure NetApp Files cross-zone-region replication (CZRR)
items.description:
Cross-zone-region replication builds on the existing capabilities of cross-region replication and cross-zone replication. It enables you to replicate volumes across regions and across availability zones within the same region, combining disaster recovery and business continuance capabilities for volumes. To establish two protection volumes, you create a cross-zone replication relationship, and a cross-region replication relationship, two cross-region replication relationships or two cross-zone replication relationships. The source volume should be in an availability zone for the cross-zone replication relationship.  

This feature is now GA and available in these Regions 

 

Learn more: 

  • What's new in Azure NetApp Files   

  • Azure Availability Zones 

  • Create a CZRR for Azure NetApp Files

items.title: Update: The retirement date for default outbound access has been extended to March 31, 2026.
items.description:
The retirement date for default outbound access has been extended to March 31, 2026. This change aligns with the broader Azure Virtual Network (VNet) update and replaces the previously communicated September 30, 2025 date. 

Starting March 31, 2026, newly created VNets will default to using private subnets. This means: 

  • Explicit outbound connectivity (e.g., via NAT Gateway, UDR, or other methods) must be configured to access public endpoints on the Internet or Microsoft services. 

  • Default outbound access will be disabled by default, but not removed. Customers who do not configure an outbound method will lose internet connectivity from their Batch nodes. 

  • Review your current Batch pool configurations, especially those using simplified node communication without public IPs.

  • Plan to implement an explicit outbound method before the March 2026 deadline. 

Learn more:

  • Read Default Internet outbound access for Simplified node communication Batch pools without public IP addresses will be retired on 30 September 2025.

  • Read How and when default outbound access is provided

  • Read Feature Update: Default behavior for newly created virtual networks will be private

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Databricks Dashboard subscriptions now support Microsoft Teams
items.description:
You can now receive insights where collaboration happens—in Microsoft Teams—with expanded dashboard subscription capabilities in Azure Databricks. This enhancement delivers timely, actionable data directly into team workflows, reducing the need to check email or switch tools. It supports faster decision-making and keeps everyone aligned in real time. As part of the broader Microsoft vision to unify data, AI, and collaboration, this feature helps you connect insights to action within the Microsoft 365 ecosystem. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Sphere OS version 25.12 is now available for evaluation
items.description:
Azure Sphere OS version 25.12 is now available for evaluation in the Retail Eval feed. Whilst this release encompasses no customer-facing changes, it represents significant under-the-hood build system changes, as such, this release will operate for an extended evaluation period, until February 2026, enabling additional time for customer evaluation testing.

Following this period, a second evaluation release, 26.02, will be launched to the Retail Eval feed for the standard 14-day testing period, and subsequently promoted to the Retail feed. This means that 25.12 will not be promoted to the Retail feed, and that the next Retail release will be 26.02.

During this time, please verify that your applications and devices operate properly with both the 25.12, and subsequent 26.02 release, before it is deployed broadly to devices in the Retail feed. 

The 25.12 OS Retail Eval release includes significant underlying build system updates.

Learn more:

  • For more information on Azure Sphere OS feeds and setting up an evaluation device group, see Azure Sphere OS feeds and Set up devices for OS evaluation.
  • For self-help inquiries or technical support, review the Azure Sphere support options.

items.title: Generally Available: FIPS compliant mode for Application Gateway V2 SKUs
items.description:
The Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 140-2 is a US government standard that defines minimum security requirements for cryptographic modules in information technology products and systems. 

Azure Application Gateway V2 now supports FIPS mode, which can be enabled during deployment or at any time afterward. When FIPS mode is turned on, the gateway uses only FIPS-compliant predefined and custom TLS policies, enhancing security and helping meet FedRAMP security requirements. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Zonal placement for Azure file shares Azure Files Premium LRS in select regions.
items.description:
Zonal Placement for Azure Files Premium LRS is now GA in select regions! This capability gives you explicit control over zone locality by pinning storage accounts to a specific availability zone, enabling high availability, fault isolation, and predictable low-latency performance for mission-critical workloads. Why it matters: Align compute and storage in the same zone for 10–40% lower latency compared to cross-zone deployments. Design resilient architectures with zone-aware control for better fault isolation.
Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Mistral Large 3 in Foundry
items.description:
Mistral Large 3, a frontier-class open-weight model with Apache 2.0 licensing, is now available in Microsoft Foundry on Azure. This model delivers enterprise-grade reliability, long-context comprehension, and multimodal reasoning—making it ideal for production assistants, retrieval-augmented applications, agentic systems, and multimodal workflows.

Key Capabilities:

  • Highly reliable instruction following
  • Extended context support for long documents and multi-turn conversations
  • Strong multimodal reasoning (text, images, diagrams)
  • Stable, predictable performance for enterprise workloads
  • Fully open and exportable for hybrid or on-premises deployment

Why it matters:
Mistral Large 3 sets a new benchmark for open models, combining frontier-level capability, reproducible results, and worldwide availability without regional restrictions. Organizations can fine-tune, customize, and deploy the model across cloud, edge, or sovereign environments with no attribution requirements.

Pricing:

  • Input: $0.50 per 1M tokens
  • Output: $1.50 per 1M tokens
  • Deployment: Global Standard (West US 3)
Learn more.

items.title: Generally Availaible: Azure MCP Server support for Azure confidential ledger
items.description:
The Azure MCP (Model Context Protocol) Server provides a streamlined approach for managing Azure resources—including Azure confidential ledger—through natural language prompts. This feature allows users to interact with confidential ledger without the need to memorize complex command syntax. Customers can now create an immutable and integrity-protected Azure confidential ledger for logging purposes. Additionally, writing to and reading from the ledger using AI is now fully supported and ready for deployment.


You can connect to Azure MCP Server utilizing a range of tools, programming languages, and frameworks. The server facilitates resource management via natural language conversations, supports the development of automation scripts, and enables integration of Azure operations into various applications. This capability is accessible through Visual Studio Code and GitHub Copilot.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Serverless workspaces in Azure Databricks
items.description:
Serverless workspaces in Azure Databricks are now available in Public Preview, offering a fully managed workspace type that comes preconfigured with serverless compute and default storage to deliver an enterprise-ready SaaS experience with minimal infrastructure setup. With this release, customers can create Azure Databricks “Serverless” workspaces directly from the Azure portal to run production workloads entirely on serverless compute, rapidly spin up short-lived environments for training and testing, and empower admins who lack direct cloud provisioning permissions to deploy and manage secure, governed Azure Databricks environments at scale. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Blob Storage SFTP - Resumable Uploads
items.description:
Announcing the general availability of resumable uploads for Azure Storage Blob SFTP. In the event of a failed partial transfer, this new feature enables users to open the partial file and continue writing the remaining content. This capability optimizes time and conserves network bandwidth, especially in situations where network interruptions occur during file transfers, such as in remote areas with low connectivity or when transferring large files like multimedia or seismic data etc.  

Resume Upload  

The resumable upload feature for Azure Blob Storage SFTP is now generally available. This feature allows users to resume file uploads from the point of failure in the event of partial transfer failures, thereby saving time and reducing network bandwidth usage.  

Learn more. 

The SFTP transfer modes that Azure Blob Storage SFTP supports are below: 

  • Write: This mode lets the client continue an upload by adding data to an existing file from a specific point without creating a new file.  
  • Write + Create: This mode allows the client to resume an upload by either adding to an existing file or creating a new one if it doesn't exist, providing flexibility when the file may not be present initially.  
  • Append: This mode adds data to the end of an existing file without overwriting its current contents.  

Resumable upload enhances efficiency by saving time and bandwidth during interrupted file transfers. Please reach out to blobsftp@microsoft.com for feedback about SFTP for Azure Blob Storage.

items.title: Retirement: Remove dependency on these Azure ML SDKs before June 30, 2026
items.description:
On June 30, 2026, AzureML SDK V1 will reach end of life. The following SDKs which work in tandem with the AzureML SDK V1 will also be retired.  

  • azureml-train-core  

  • azureml-pipeline  

  • azureml-pipeline-core  

  • azureml-pipeline-internal  

  • azureml-pipeline-steps  

After June 30, 2026, you can continue to use these SDKs, however they will not be supported and may stop working without notice.  

Recommended action  

To ensure that you are using a supported SDK for your workloads, it is recommended to migrate to AzureML SDK V1 before 30 Jun 2026.  

Detailed guidance is documented here.

Help and support  

If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A. If you have a support plan and you need technical help, create a support case.  

Links provided herein may take you to a third-party website and are provided for convenience only. Third-party websites are subject to the third-party's terms and privacy statements.  

Learn more about service retirements that may impact your resources in the Azure Retirement Workbook. Please note that retirements may not be visible in the workbook for up to two weeks after being announced.

Now you can install the credcheck extension in Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server. The credcheck extension helps you to enforce password and credential validation policies directly within PostgreSQL.

items.description:
Now you can deploy Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server in the Belgium Central Azure region.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Load Balancer bandwidth metrics now support Protocol dimension
items.description:
Bandwidth metrics for Azure Load Balancer are now published with metric dimension Protocol. When retrieving or viewing Byte, Packet, and SYN Count metrics in the Azure portal, you will now see the dimension Protocol. TCP traffic is denoted by Protocol=6, while UDP traffic is represented by Protocol=17. 

With the Protocol dimension, you gain more granular visibility into traffic patterns for alerting, monitoring, and troubleshooting requirements. 

The Protocol dimension is available on Byte, Packet, and SYN Count metrics in all Azure public regions, China cloud regions, and Government cloud regions. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Perth - Azure Extended Zones
items.description:
We are announcing the general availability of the Perth Azure Extended Zone.   

Azure Extended Zones are small-footprint extensions of Azure placed in metro areas, industry centers, or specific jurisdictions, to serve low latency and data residency workloads. They support a selection of virtual machine (VMs), container, networking, storage, and other Azure services. Azure Extended Zones can run latency-sensitive and throughput-intensive applications close to end users, within data residency boundaries.  

Learn more about onboarding and managing Azure Extended Zones on our learn page, and start unlocking low-latency performance for your Perth workloads.

items.title: Public Preview: Managed Identity support in Network Watcher VNET flow log, traffic analytics and packet capture
items.description:
VNET flow log captures IP traffic flowing through VNETs, subnets, and NICs for monitoring, troubleshooting, network optimization, security, and compliance needs and stores the logs in Azure Storage 

Traffic Analytics leverages VNET flow logs and aggregates, processes and enriches the flows to analyze traffic flow and offers insights into network activity, visualization, security, and performance. 

Network Watcher packet capture enables the capture of network packets directly from a virtual machine, helping users perform deep network analysis and diagnose issues. 

Managed identities provided by Microsoft Entra ID enables VNET flow logs and traffic analytics to securely access Azure Blob Storage and log analytics workspace respectively without the need to manage credentials. For more information, see What is managed identities for Azure resources. 

After you enable managed identity for Network Watcher VNET flow logs, traffic analytics, or packet capture by granting the managed identity necessary permissions will use the managed identity to obtain an access token from Microsoft Entra ID for accessing the specified resource.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Claude Opus 4.5 Available in Microsoft Foundry
items.description:
Claude Opus 4.5 is now available in public preview on Microsoft Foundry, bringing advanced coding, agentic workflows, and enterprise productivity to Azure customers. Claude Opus 4.5 sets a new benchmark for performance and versatility, outperforming previous Claude models and delivering frontier intelligence at a more accessible price point. With seamless integration into Foundry Models, Playground, and Agent Service, organizations can build and scale AI solutions securely and efficiently. The model benefits from Azure’s enterprise-grade security and compliance, and supports use cases from software development to financial analysis and cybersecurity. Pricing starts at $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens, available in East US2 and Sweden Central regions. Get started today in the Foundry portal. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure File Sync in New Zealand North
items.description:
Azure File Sync enables seamless tiering of data from on-premises Windows Servers to Azure Files for hybrid use cases and simplified migration. It also enables you to leverage the performance, flexibility and compatibility of your on-premises File Server while leveraging the scale and cost effectiveness of Azure Files.

The expansion into New Zealand North brings the service closer to organizations in these regions, offering lower latency, better performance, and support for local data residency requirements.

If Azure File Sync is not yet available in your preferred region, please fill out this survey to express interest.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Entra ID support for RDP connections
items.description:
Announcing Azure Bastion now supports Microsoft Entra ID authentication for RDP connections to Windows VMs directly in the portal. 

This update brings two key benefits for RDP users connecting to their virtual machines: 

  • Enhanced Security: By eliminating local authentication mechanisms, this feature reduces potential attack surfaces, helping customers strengthen their security posture. 
  • Seamless Access: With Microsoft Entra ID as the authentication method, users enjoy a simple, one-click sign-on experience—no extra credentials required. 

This is a big step forward in making secure and streamlined VM access easier than ever. 

Learn more:

  • about Microsoft Entra ID.

  • about Entra ID for RDP connections.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure MCP Server for Azure Database for MySQL
items.description:
Announcing that Azure MCP Server now supports Azure Database for MySQL. With this update, you can empower AI agents and applications to interact with your MySQL data using natural language through the open Model Context Protocol (MCP). Instead of writing complex queries, you can simply ask questions like “retrieve schema details for the customers table,” “show the last 7 days of failed orders,” or “summarize anomalies by region.” These interactions support Microsoft Entra authentication, eliminating password management and ensuring enterprise-grade security. 

 

By integrating MySQL tools into the Azure MCP Server alongside other services such as Azure AI Search, Azure Cosmos DB, and Azure Storage, you gain a unified interface for building intelligent, context-aware workflows. This consistency reduces integration complexity, accelerates development, and enables you to create agentic solutions that span data exploration, analysis, and operational actions—all within the trusted Azure ecosystem. 

 

You benefit from faster insights, simplified schema discovery, and the ability to automate MySQL-driven business logic without leaving your development environment. 

 

Get started today by installing Azure MCP Server in Visual Studio Code, enabling GitHub Copilot, and setting up Microsoft Entra authentication for Azure Database for MySQL. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Regex support in T-SQL
items.description:
Boost your SQL queries with powerful regular expressions (regex) support for advanced pattern matching. Now you can use native regex in T-SQL directly in Azure SQL and SQL Server 2025 queries—simplifying code, improving maintainability, and reducing dependency on external scripts. 

Learn more

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Load Testing in Italy North
items.description:
Azure Load Testing capability in Azure App Testing is now generally available in Italy North. Customers can now use Azure Load Testing, a fully managed load-testing service to generate high scale load and run simulations, easily identify performance bottlenecks through a rich dashboard of client-side and server-side metrics, get AI powered actionable insights, and integrate load tests into their CI/CD workflows. Customers can get started without any knowledge of load-testing tools, or use their existing Apache JMeter or Locust scripts.

Learn more:
  • about Azure Load Testing.
  • go to feedback forum.

items.title: Generally Available: Custom handler support in Azure Functions Flex consumption
items.description:
Azure Functions now supports custom handlers in Flex consumption. Custom handlers are lightweight web servers that receive events from the Functions host. Any language that supports HTTP primitives can implement a custom handler. 

 

Custom handlers are best suited for situations where you want to: 

  • Implement a function app in a language that's not currently offered out-of-the box, such as Go or Rust. 
  • Implement a function app in a runtime that's not currently featured by default, such as Deno.  

With custom handlers, you can use triggers and input and output bindings via extension bundles. 

Learn more:

  • Get started with Azure Functions custom handlers with quickstarts in Go and Rust.
  • Review the documentation.

items.title: Retirement: Migrate to dedicated VM for your compute clusters
items.description:
On September 30, 2025, Low-Priority VM will reach end of life. However, you will continue to be supported on Azure Machine Learning until March 31, 2026.  

To ensure that your clusters are not automatically scaled down it is recommended to migrate to dedicated VMs before that date.  

After March 31, 2026, you'll not be able to use your clusters with low-priority VM.  

 

Required action  

To ensure you're using a supported cluster, you can recreate your low-priority VM clusters with dedicated VM before March 31, 2026.  

Detailed guidance is documented here 

Help and support  

If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A. If you have a support plan and you need technical help, create a support case.  

Links provided herein may take you to a third-party website and are provided for convenience only. Third-party websites are subject to the third-party's terms and privacy statements.  

Learn more about service retirements that may impact your resources in the Azure Retirement Workbook. Please note that retirements may not be visible in the workbook for up to two weeks after being announced.

items.title: Public Preview: Container network metrics filtering in Advanced Container Networking Services for (ACNS) for AKS
items.description:
Container network metrics filtering in Azure Container Networking Services (ACNS) is now available in public preview.

 

In containerized environments, the ingestion of excessive network metrics can lead to inflated storage costs and cluttered dashboards, making it difficult to maintain observability efficiency. Azure Container Networking Services (ACNS) now offers container network metrics filtering, available in public preview, to address this challenge. 

This new capability enables users to define fine-grained filters at the Cilium level using a Custom Resource Definition (CRD), allowing metrics collection to be scoped by namespace or pod. By filtering metrics before they reach Prometheus, organizations can significantly reduce data volume, lower operational overhead, and improve the clarity of their observability tools.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: MCP support for AI toolchain operator add-on in AKS
items.description:
MCP support for AI toolchain operator add-on is now Generally Available.   

 

The AI Toolchain Operator add-on now supports KAITO inference workspaces with integrated tool calling and Model Context Protocol (MCP), addressing key challenges around dynamic model interaction and real-time data integration.  

 

Previously, developers faced friction deploying LLM-based services that needed external tool access, such as APIs or custom functions, often requiring bespoke orchestration. Now, you can benefit from seamless integration of KAITO’s vLLM-based tool calling with supported models, along with MCP support for connecting models to external systems in real time – to enable smarter, more context-aware AI services directly within AKS. 

Learn more:

  • about Integrate tool calling with LLM Inference with the AI toolchain operator add-on on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
  • about Integrate an MCP server with an LLM Inference Service on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)

items.title: Generally Available: Local redirect policy in Azure CNI powered by Cilium for AKS
items.description:
Local redirect policy with Azure CNI powered by Cilium for AKS is now generally available. 

Customers running high-scale AKS workloads often experience latency and performance bottlenecks due to cross-node traffic routing. The new local redirect policy addresses this by enabling node-local service routing, ensuring traffic is redirected to pods on the same node whenever possible. This results in lower latency, improved throughput, and enhanced reliability, especially critical for AI training and microservice-based applications.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Cluster-wide Cilium network policy with Azure CNI powered by Cilium for AKS
items.description:
Cluster-wide Cilium network policy for AKS clusters using Azure CNI powered by Cilium is now Generally Available.  

 

Managing consistent network policies across Kubernetes namespaces has long been a challenge for platform teams, especially in multi-tenant environments. With the general availability of cluster-wide Cilium network policy for AKS clusters using Azure CNI powered by Cilium, customers can now define and enforce network policies at the cluster level. This enhancement simplifies policy management and strengthens isolation between tenants by leveraging Cilium’s high-performance eBPF dataplane. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure NetApp Files single file restore from backup
items.description:
With Azure NetApp Files single file restore from backup, you can restore individual files from Azure NetApp Files backup vault without needing to restore an entire volume. By restoring only the necessary files, you can save time and cost needed for restoring data. This feature is available in all ANF supported region. 
Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Layer 7 policy with Advanced Container Networking Services (ACNS) for AKS
items.description:
To address the growing need for granular traffic control in microservices architectures, Azure Container Networking Services now offers Layer 7 Policy as a generally available feature. This capability empowers customers to enforce fine-grained traffic controls at the application layer, supporting protocols such as HTTP, HTTPS, gRPC, and Kafka. By bridging gaps in zero-trust enforcement and microservice isolation, Layer 7 Policy enhances security posture, provides deeper traffic visibility, and simplifies policy management, all without compromising performance. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: DNS security policy Threat Intelligence feed
items.description:
Azure DNS security policy Threat Intelligence feed is now generally available. Protect against known malicious domains with Microsoft’s managed Threat Intelligent feed. 

 

Smart Protection 

 

  • Almost all attacks begin with a DNS query. Threat Intelligence managed domain list enables you to detect and prevent security incidents early. 

 

 Continuous Updates 


  • The feed is automatically updated by Microsoft so that you stay protected against newly detected malicious domains.  

 

Monitor and Block 

  • You have the flexibility of just observing the activity in Alert only mode or block the suspected activity in blocking mode.  
  • Enabling logging feature gives you visibility into all DNS traffic in the virtual network.
Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Sphere OS version 25.10 is now available
items.description:
Azure Sphere OS version 25.10 is now available in the Retail feed. This release includes updates to Azure Sphere OS only; it does not include an updated SDK. If your devices are connected to the internet, they will receive the updated OS from the cloud.

This release includes quality and underlying build system updates.

For self-help inquiries or technical support, review the Azure Sphere support options.

items.title: Generally Available: Trusted Launch is now supported for Arm64 Marketplace Images
items.description:
Announcing that Trusted Launch supported Arm64 Images are now available in the Azure Marketplace. You can now get the dual benefit of cost and performance efficiencies of Arm64 in addition to the security benefits of Trusted Launch. 

 

Arm64 VMs bring cost savings, energy efficiency, and high performance to cloud workloads. 

 

Trusted Launch VMs provide foundational compute security to Azure VMs by enabling Secure Boot and vTPM capabilities. Trusted Launch protects OS against rootkits, boot kits and enables attestation by measuring the boot chain of VM. 

 

The Cobalt 100 based Arm64 VMs (Dpsv6/Dplsv6/Epsv6) support the Trusted Launch security type, and users can improve the security of their Cobalt 100 VMs by deploying with Trusted Launch images from the marketplace. Supported images include Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, Rocky 9, Azure Linux 3, RedHat Enterprise Linux 10, and more. 

Learn more:

  • about Trusted Launch.
  • about Cobalt 100 VMs.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure NetApp Files cache volumes
items.description:
Azure NetApp Files cache volumes are now available in public preview. The cache volumes feature is a new capability built on NetApp’s ONTAP FlexCache technology that provides a persistent, high-performance cache in Azure for data stored on ONTAP-based storage volumes outside of Azure NetApp Files. This feature enables organizations to cache active (“hot”) data closer to users and cloud applications, dramatically improving data access speeds and throughput over WAN connections. With cache volumes, you can burst on-premises datasets to Azure with near-local performance, which is ideal for scenarios such as running computational workloads in Azure or enabling globally distributed teams to collaborate without file transfer delays.   

 

Cache volumes is available in these regions. 

 

Learn more:   

  • What's new in Azure NetApp Files 

  • Configure a cache volume for Azure NetApp Files

items.title: Public Preview: Azure NetApp Files migration assistant (portal support)
items.description:
Azure NetApp Files migration assistant (with SnapMirror) provides efficient and cost-effective data migration leveraging ONTAP's built-in replication engine for seamless transition from on-premises or CVO/other cloud providers to Azure NetApp Files (ANF). This feature offers benefits aligned with the goal to accelerate and simplify migrations of business-critical applications and data to Azure. The feature is now available in Azure Portal and is now in Public Preview in all regions. 

 

Key Benefits 

  • Storage-efficient data transfer that reduces network transfer costs for both baseline and incremental updates 

  • Low cutover/downtime window ensuring faster and more efficient final updates, minimizing disruption to customer operations 

  • Volume migration using migration assistant includes source volume snapshots for primary data protection, and directory and file metadata maintaining security attributes 

Learn more: 

  • What’s new 

  • Migrate volumes to Azure NetApp Files | Microsoft Learn

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Monitor for Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes with OpenShift and Azure Red Hat OpenShift
items.description:
Azure Monitor provides a complete set of services for monitoring the health and performance of different layers of your Kubernetes infrastructure and the applications that depend on it.

Azure Monitor now supports Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes with OpenShift and Azure Red Hat OpenShift with Container Insights and Managed Prometheus.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: 20 MB/s/TiB Performance Tier for Azure Managed Lustre
items.description:
Azure Managed Lustre now offers a new 20 MB/s/TiB performance tier in public preview, designed to meet the demands of large-scale AI and high-performance computing (HPC) workloads. This tier enables customers to provision file systems up to 25 PiB in a single namespace, delivering up to 512 GB/s of bandwidth and supporting up to 20 billion inodes for massive file counts.

The 20 MB/s/TiB tier uses Lustre’s DNE2 multi-MDS architecture, adding one MDS per 5 PiB to enable directory striping across multiple metadata targets. This boosts metadata operations, delivering over 5× higher IOPS in mdtest benchmarks as striping scales. Ideal for AI training and HPC workloads, it ensures high metadata throughput and efficient handling of massive datasets.

By offering a lower bandwidth density option, customers can optimize costs while scaling to larger namespaces, consolidating workloads into a single, high-performance file system and simplifying their architecture.

To request access to the public preview, please fill out this form.

items.title: Generally Available: CSI Dynamic Provisioning for Azure Managed Lustre
items.description:
CSI Dynamic Provisioning for Azure Managed Lustre (AMLFS) is now generally available. With dynamic provisioning, Kubernetes applications can request AMLFS-backed persistent volumes on demand using standard StorageClass and PersistentVolumeClaim objects—no pre‑provisioning of volumes is required. This simplifies day-to-day operations for AI/ML training, simulation, and high‑throughput analytics that rely on POSIX file semantics and shared access at scale.

This GA supports Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) clusters running Kubernetes 1.21 and later and uses the Azure Lustre CSI driver. Dynamic provisioning is supported in driver version v0.3.0 and later. Node pools must use the Ubuntu Linux OS SKU.

Administrators define a StorageClass that references an AMLFS file system; developers then bind PVCs to create AMLFS volumes automatically. The driver integrates with the AMLFS client (Lustre 2.15.x) and follows the Kubernetes CSI specification.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Managed Lustre Support for Azure MCP Server
items.description:
Azure Managed Lustre now offers full integration with Azure MCP Server, and this capability is generally available. Azure MCP Server enables developers and infrastructure teams to manage Azure resources—including Azure Managed Lustre file systems—using natural language prompts, streamlining operations for AI training and high-performance computing (HPC) environments.

With this integration, you can create, list, and manage Azure Managed Lustre file systems directly from supported IDEs (such as Visual Studio Code, Visual Studio, and IntelliJ) or via automation scripts, using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The Azure Managed Lustre tools for MCP Server support advanced configuration options, including specifying network, capacity, maintenance windows, availability zones, and encryption settings. This makes it easier to provision and operate scalable, high-performance Lustre file systems for large-scale simulation, model training, and fine-tuning workloads.

Azure MCP Server provides secure, role-based access and supports a wide range of Azure services, enabling unified management and automation for modern AI and HPC pipelines.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Auto-import for Azure Managed Lustre
items.description:
The Auto-import feature for Azure Managed Lustre (AMLFS) is now available in public preview. Auto-import enables seamless, policy-driven synchronization of data from Azure Blob Storage containers into AMLFS clusters, automatically reflecting new, changed, or deleted blobs in the Lustre namespace. This feature supports hybrid workflows where data is generated in Blob and consumed in AMLFS.

Customers can configure import policies per Blob container–AMLFS cluster pair, specifying which types of changes are imported and how conflicts are resolved. This flexibility supports a range of scenarios, including post-deployment ingestion, machine learning pipelines, and continuous data synchronization for analytics workloads. Auto-import helps unify object and file-based workflows, enabling near real-time data sharing and reducing operational overhead by eliminating the need for manual import scripts or intermediate file servers.

Operational efficiency is further enhanced by allowing customers to select conflict resolution policies and control whether deletions in Blob are reflected in AMLFS. These capabilities provide native integration with Azure Blob Storage and the Azure ecosystem.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Recommended alerts for Azure Monitor Workspace
items.description:
Azure Monitor now offers one-click enablement of recommended alerts directly in the Azure Portal for Azure Monitor Managed service for Prometheus customers. These alerts enable you to monitor the ingestion limits for Azure Monitor Workspace and avoid metrics throttling.
Learn more

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Managed Redis integration with Microsoft Foundry
items.description:
Azure Managed Redis is now available as part of the Microsoft Foundry MCP tools catalog, allowing customers to use Redis as a knowledge store or memory store for AI agents. This integration makes it simple to connect Redis to Foundry-based agents, enabling semantic searching, long term and short term memory, and faster reasoning for multi-agent applications—all running on trusted Azure infrastructure.

Learn more:
  • About Azure Managed Redis.
  • About what's new in Azure Managed Redis.
  • Try Azure Managed Redis samples on GitHub

items.title: Public Preview: Azure API Management adds support for A2A Agent APIs
items.description:
Announcing the public preview of A2A API support in Azure API Management. With this new capability, organizations can manage and govern agent APIs alongside other API types — AI model APIs, Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, and traditional APIs such as REST, SOAP, and GraphQL. 

This update empowers customers to extend their established API governance and security practices into the evolving agentic ecosystem, strengthening secure access, enforcing policies consistently, and ensuring observability for AI agents.
