A2A APIs in Azure API Management offer advanced mediation of JSON-RPC runtime operations with robust policy support, enable agent card exposure to agents, users, or clients, and provide comprehensive tracing aligned with the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic convention. 

Additionally, you now have the option to register A2A APIs in Azure API Center, enabling organization-wide discovery and governance of agent APIs. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Databricks Genie in Copilot Studio
items.description:
Azure Databricks Genie is now available in Microsoft Copilot Studio, giving you direct access to intelligent, enterprise-grade AI answers across your full Azure Databricks data estate. This integration unlocks enterprise-grade, conversational analytics across your data estate—no code required. Through Model Context Protocol (MCP), Copilot Studio agents can now deliver richer, more accurate responses grounded in your actual business data. You can instantly publish Genie-powered agents to Microsoft Teams and Microsoft 365 to accelerate decision-making and empower users at every level. 

 

Bringing Azure Databricks Genie capabilities into daily collaboration helps your teams save time, reduce errors, and eliminate barriers to advanced analytics. The unified platform amplifies your ability to act quickly and drive better outcomes, all while reinforcing the value of open, extensible interoperability across the Microsoft ecosystem.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Microsoft Foundry data connection for Azure Databricks
items.description:
Azure Databricks Genie is now integrated with Microsoft Foundry and in public preview. You can now connect Genie spaces directly to Microsoft Foundry agents using Model Context Protocol (MCP), giving you seamless access to trusted data for building intelligent workflows.  

 

This release simplifies AI development by streamlining data connectivity, boosting governance, and accelerating time-to-value. You can spend less time setting up your data environment and more time building intelligent solutions that take advantage of the Microsoft unified platform for data, AI, and governance to drive business value. 

 

Whether you're scaling AI or unifying your data strategy, integration of Genie and Microsoft Foundry helps you do more—securely and efficiently. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: TLS and TCP termination on Azure Application Gateway
items.description:
Azure Application Gateway has introduced general availability support for TLS and TCP protocol termination. This enhancement enables you to load balance and securely process non-HTTP(S) traffic for applications that rely on TCP or TLS protocols. The gateway terminates the incoming connection at the proxy and establishes a new connection to the backend servers. The TLS certificate management is available for both HTTPS and TLS protocols on a resource, simplifying the certificate operations and providing a single endpoint for clients. 

With this release, the TLS/TCP proxy also brings support for Client IP preservation using the PROXY protocol header, as well as support for port 22 on listeners. 

This capability is available on Application Gateway Standard v2 and WAF v2 SKUs. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Claude in Microsoft Foundry
items.description: Claude models by Anthropic are now available for Public Preview in Microsoft Foundry, expanding the platform’s unified ecosystem of frontier AI. Enterprises can access Claude Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.1, and Haiku 4.5 for advanced long-context reasoning, coding, and multimodal comprehension—integrated across Foundry Models, Playground, and Agent Service. Importantly, Claude is offered within the global standard deployment type, ensuring that organizations can leverage these models with consistent availability, enterprise-grade support, and compliance across worldwide Azure regions. This makes it straightforward for customers to deploy and scale Claude-powered solutions wherever they operate, benefiting from Microsoft’s trusted infrastructure and governance. This launch marks a major milestone in Microsoft’s open, interoperable AI strategy, empowering customers to build agentic systems, automate workflows, and ground Claude in enterprise data with full observability, security, and Responsible AI. With Claude joining over 11,000 other models, Foundry offers the broadest model choice and seamless integration with Azure services, making it the only enterprise platform to unify all major model families in one governed environment.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Copilot agents - a closer look at the deployment agent
items.description:
Following our Azure Copilot announcement introducing agentic capabilities, this update focuses on one of the six new agents: the deployment agent. The deployment agent helps you discover, plan, and deploy cloud workloads faster and with confidence using natural language guidance. Through ongoing dialogues, the deployment agent captures requirements and delivers real-time guidance to plan and deploy workloads, reducing complexity and errors.  

Using the Azure Well-Architected Framework, the agent recommends best-practice architectures and offers tailored suggestions—from optimal pre-built templates to custom IaC—ensuring deployments are fast, intuitive, and robust.  

With the Azure Copilot deployment agent, users benefit from:  

  • Intelligent workload recommendations based on Azure’s Well Architected Framework pillars.  
  • Step-by-step guidance for planning and deploying infrastructure.  
  • Optimal pre-built template selection or customized IaC that meets user needs.  
  • Ability to pull custom IaC to users Git Hub repositories or VS Code Web based deployment.   

To access Azure Copilot’s agents, including this one, please use this form.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Managed Instance on Azure App Service
items.description:
Announcing Managed Instance on Azure App Service, now in Public Preview! This new capability makes it easy to move web apps to the cloud with minimal configuration—no code rewrites required. Whether your .NET apps run on-premises or in VMs, you can move to a fully managed PaaS environment, future-proof your infrastructure, and unlock cloud benefits.

Why Managed Instance?

Many organizations still rely on older .NET apps for critical tasks like billing, HR, compliance, and reporting. These apps often depend on Windows-specific features and custom tools, which makes rewriting them expensive and risky. With Managed Instance on Azure App Service, they can keep operating with critical dependencies on local Windows services, third-party vendor libraries, and custom runtimes without requiring any code changes. The result is faster app modernization with lower overhead, and access to cloud-native scalability, built-in security and Azure’s AI capabilities.

Key Benefits:

  • Full App Service experience with turnkey scaling, resiliency, and integrated services.
  • Greater control via RDP access through Bastion, custom configurations, and identity management.
  • Compatibility for complex workloads, including classic .NET Framework apps, without code changes.

As part of a holistic migration and modernization strategy, Managed Instance simplifies app modernization, reduces costs, and accelerates your journey to the cloud.

items.title: Public Preview: Smart Tier account level tiering (Azure Blob Storage and ADLS)
items.description:
Introducing smart tier Public Preview for account level tiering 

Announcing the public preview of smart tier for Azure Blob Storage and Azure Data Lake Storage (ADLS). Smart tier is a fully managed and automated data tiering solution, avoiding manual tier placement for object storage standard online tiers. 

Smart tier automatically moves your data between hot, cool, and cold access tiers based on usage patterns, optimizing your costs for these access tiers automatically. New data is stored in the hot tier. Any object that isn’t accessed for 30 days is moved to the cool tier; after 90 days of inactivity, it transitions to the cold tier. If objects are accessed, they are transitioning back to the hot tier and restart their tiering cycle. 

Key Capabilities 

  • Seamless Enablement: Activate smart tier at the storage account scope on new and existing general purpose v2 storage accounts with zonal redundancies today.  
  • Automated Lifecycle: Data movement between tiers is fully automated. Smart tier ensures optimal tier placement for both your active and inactive objects.
  • Simplified Billing Model: Your data uses the existing hot, cool and cold tier capacity prices. There are no charges for tier transitions inside smart tier, early deletion or data retrieval fees. A monitoring fee Is charged for objects stored in smart tier over 128 KiB in size. 

Learn more.

products: GitHub Advanced Security for Azure DevOps
items.title: Public Preview: Microsoft Defender for Cloud + GitHub Advanced Security
items.description: With Microsoft Defender for Cloud and GitHub Advanced Security, protect cloud-native applications across the full app lifecycle from code to cloud. This natively integrated solution helps unify developers and security teams in one workflow while staying in the tools they use every day. Identify vulnerabilities early and connect live threat insights from production environments directly to the vulnerabilities that matter to help prioritize risks. And with Copilot Autofix and the Coding agent, developer teams can apply AI-suggested fixes in minutes, reducing remediation time.

items.title: Generally Available: Private Marketplace for VS Code
items.description:
The VS Code Private Marketplace is a secure, enterprise-ready way to host and manage extensions internally—fully integrated with VS Code. 

Teams can self-host, deploy easily, and manage updates with flexibility and control.

Learn more.

items.title: Private Preview: Azure HorizonDB
items.description:
Engineered for performance, Azure HorizonDB for PostgreSQL delivers future-proof, autoscaling storage up to 128 TB, up to 3 times faster performance than open-source PostgreSQL, and rapid compute scalability to 3,072 vCores. Now in private preview, Azure Horizon DB is built to handle your most critical applications with enterprise-ready security and reliability. 

 

You can build smarter, scalable apps using in-database, pre-provisioned AI models; advanced capabilities like DiskANN vector indexing for fast, filtered search; and native semantic operators for intelligent query handling. Familiar PostgreSQL extensions and GitHub Copilot integration streamline development workflows, helping you move from idea to impact with speed and confidence. 

 

Seamlessly integrated into the Microsoft ecosystem, Azure HorizonDB provides easy access to advanced AI and analytics services on Azure, eliminating integration overhead.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Entra-only identities support with Azure Files SMB
items.description:
Azure Files now supports Entra-only identities, enabling customers to retire on-premises domain controllers while maintaining secure SMB access to file shares. This feature delivers a fully cloud-native authentication model using Microsoft Entra Kerberos allowing secure access for identities /groups created and managed in MS Entra. Placing identity and access control in the cloud also enhances remote and distributed workforce scenarios—no VPN or hybrid trust required.

While beneficial across all workloads, this capability is especially impactful for:
  • Information Worker collaboration (departmental shares, project folders)
  • VDI/AVD environments with FSLogix profiles
  • Industry workloads requiring secure, mobile access

Contact azurefiles@microsoft.com if you have questions or are interested in adopting Entra-only identities for Azure Files.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Application Gateway mTLS passthrough support
items.description:
Announcing a new mTLS enhancement in Azure Application Gateway for backend applications that perform client certificate and authorization header validation at the backend while still requiring web traffic inspection through the Web Application Firewall (WAF). This update introduces greater flexibility by allowing such applications to accept and inspect traffic through the Application Gateway even when a client certificate is not presented, supporting mixed authentication scenarios with both mTLS and token-based access.

What Changed

Previously, Application Gateway listeners operated in Strict mode, blocking any connection without a valid client certificate. This meant traffic relying solely on authorization tokens could not reach the backend.

With this update, you can now enable Passthrough mode for mutual TLS (mTLS) connections, allowing:

  • Requests without client certificates to pass through WAF for inspection.
  • Backend applications to retain full control over certificate and token validation logic.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: JWT Validation in Azure Application Gateway
items.description:
Announcing the preview of JSON Web Token (JWT) validation in Azure Application Gateway — enabling authentication and token validation right at the Application gateway before traffic reaches your backend applications or APIs.

Why It matters

  • Protect at the perimeter: Block requests with missing or invalid tokens (401/403) at the edge, ensuring only trusted traffic reaches your services.

  • Boost performance: Offload token validation from your microservices or web apps to improve scalability and response times.

  • Simplify operations: Apply consistent authentication policies centrally across multiple applications and routes.

What’s included in the preview

  • Issuer (iss) validation

  • Audience (aud) matching - supports Client ID and/or custom App ID URIs

  • Expiration (exp) enforcement

  • Signature verification using JWKS

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Premium Ingress in Azure Container Apps
items.description:
Azure Container Apps support for premium ingress is now generally available. This feature introduces environment-level ingress configuration options, with the primary highlight being customizable ingress scaling. This capability supports the scaling of the ingress proxy, enabling customers to better handle higher demand workloads, such as large performance tests. By configuring your ingress proxy to run on workload profiles, you can scale out more ingress instances to handle more load. Running the ingress proxy on a workload profile will incur associated costs.  


To further enhance the flexibility of your application, this release includes other ingress-related settings, such as termination grace period, idle request timeout, and header count. 


Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Rule-based routing in Azure Container Apps
items.description:
Azure Container Apps support for rule-based routing is now generally available. This feature provides greater flexibility and composability to your Azure Container Apps by simplifying your architecture for microservice applications, A/B testing, blue-green deployments, and more.  

Rule-based routing allows you to direct incoming HTTP traffic to different apps within your Container Apps environment based on the requested host name or path. This includes support for custom domains. Instead of having to configure a separate reverse proxy, such as NGINX, you can now provide routing rules for your environment and incoming traffic will automatically be routed to the specified target apps. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Deployment labels in Azure Container Apps
items.description:
Azure Container Apps now supports deployment labels in public preview as a new deployment mode. This feature simplifies environment management and enables advanced deployment strategies for your applications by allowing you to assign meaningful names—such as dev, staging, or prod—to specific container revisions. 

Deployment labels provide a flexible way to manage traffic routing and revision control without renaming revisions or manually adjusting configurations. These include: 

  • Streamline environment management by grouping revisions under descriptive labels. 
  • Route traffic intelligently based on labels for A/B testing, staged rollouts, and blue-green deployments. 
  • Promote or roll back revisions quickly using label history, ensuring smooth transitions and minimal downtime. 
With deployment labels, you gain greater control over your application lifecycle while reducing complexity in multi-environment scenarios.   

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Dynamic sessions shell environment and MCP support in Azure Container Apps
items.description:
Azure Container Apps now supports dynamic shell sessions in public preview. A shell session is a platform-managed built-in container used to run and execute common shell commands in an isolated sandboxed environment.  


With Azure Container Apps dynamic sessions supporting empty shell sessions and an integrated MCP server, customers can instantly provide agents with secure, isolated sandboxes for tasks like code execution, tool testing, or workflow automation. This enables seamless integration into agent frameworks, allowing agents to access disposable compute environments on demand. Customers benefit from rapid provisioning, enhanced security, and reduced operational overhead for agentic workloads. 


Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure SQL updates for November 2025
items.description:
In November 2025, the following updates and enhancements were made to Azure SQL: 

  • View, modify, insert rows in a table without manually writing T-SQL code using the interactive Edit Data interface in the MSSQL extension for Visual Studio Code. Learn more. 

  • Import and export DACPACs—now available in the MSSQL extension. Apply DACPAC files to new or existing databases or generate new files from existing databases. Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure SQL updates for November 2025
items.description:
In November 2025, the following updates and enhancements were made to Azure SQL:  

  • Apply the reservation discount for a 1-year or 3-year reservation of a zone-redundant Azure SQL Managed Instance in the General Purpose tier to both the standard compute and the zone-redundancy add-on. Learn more.  

  • Optimize performance and costs by adding extra memory to Azure SQL Managed Instance. Learn more. 

  • New improvements in optimized locking further reduce the overhead of locks in the SQL database engine. Learn more.

  • Boost your SQL queries with powerful Regex support for advanced pattern matching. Learn more. 

  • Bigint support in DATEADD for extended range calculations. Learn more.

items.title: Generally Availabe: SQL Server 2025
items.description:
SQL Server 2025, the AI-ready enterprise database, is now generally available, marking a major milestone in Microsoft’s mission to modernize enterprise data platforms. This release introduces built-in AI capabilities, seamless integration with Microsoft Fabric and Azure, and enhanced developer productivity through familiar T-SQL extensions. Now you can boost performance and security using intelligent query processing, optimized concurrency, and Microsoft Entra-based identity management. 

 

SQL Server 2025 is designed for hybrid environments—on-premises, multi-cloud, and edge—delivering enterprise-grade reliability and compliance while enabling next-generation AI scenarios. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: New SQL Server migration in Azure Arc
items.description:
A new SQL Server migration in Azure Arc solution streamlines and accelerates your journey to Azure SQL Managed Instance. Powered by Azure Database Migration Service and assisted by Copilot, it delivers an automated, end-to-end migration process that includes continuous assessments, simplified provisioning, and real-time replication.

 

The capabilities in SQL Server migration in Azure Arc include:

  • Continuous assessment reporting that automatically delivers readiness, cost, and technical insights. 

  • Streamlined provisioning. You can select or provision Azure SQL targets directly within the portal, eliminating context switching. 

  • Real-time data replication via distributed availability groups (DAGs). Instead of a complex, multiple-step setup, you get a simplified replication process without the need to navigate separate portals. 

  • Read-only replica validation. You can test target instances before cutover, avoiding rework. 

  • Client connection summaries that continuously identify which clients connect to each SQL instance, replacing manual tracing. 

  • Copilot assistance and troubleshooting that guides you through the migration steps, reducing manual effort and delays. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Microsoft Python driver for SQL Server
items.description:
Announcing that the mssql-python driver is now generally available. This milestone marks a major step forward in delivering a modern, high-performance, and developer-friendly experience for Python developers working with SQL Server, Azure SQL Database, and SQL databases in Microsoft Fabric. 
Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) 22
items.description:
SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) has long been the trusted tool for managing SQL databases, writing T-SQL, and troubleshooting issues. With SSMS 22, built on Visual Studio 2026, you get support for SQL Server 2025, improved integration with SQL databases in Fabric, and native compatibility on Windows ARM64 devices. This release also introduces the GitHub Copilot preview, giving you AI-powered assistance for T-SQL authoring and optimization directly within SSMS. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure SQL Database long-term retention (LTR) backup immutability
items.description:
You can now configure immutability for Azure SQL Database LTR backups to meet compliance and regulatory needs. Once immutability is configured, the backups can’t be edited or deleted until the specified retention expires, mitigating any potential ransomware attacks for the entire retention.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: MSSQL extension integration with GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio Code
items.description:
The MSSQL extension for Visual Studio Code now integrates GitHub Copilot, bringing AI-powered SQL assistance directly into your development workflow. Together, they help you reduce repetitive tasks, accelerate development, and design database schemas and applications faster and more intelligently. With just a few clicks in Visual Studio Code, you can generate T-SQL and object-relational mapping (ORM) code, explore schemas, and build, analyze, and optimize queries—even if you’re new to SQL. 

 

This general availability release brings a more complete GitHub Copilot experience, including Ask mode, Agent mode, and slash commands. You can use natural language and interact in multiple ways with your SQL Server, Azure SQL, or SQL database in Microsoft Fabric. You also get more detailed connection information, clearer error messages, better database context awareness, and improved guidance—enhancements that make GitHub Copilot easier and more natural to use as part of your daily workflow. 

 

Whether you’re building modern web apps, cloud-native solutions, or AI-driven experiences, GitHub Copilot helps you understand the business logic within your database, follow best practices for security and performance, and even generate mock data for rapid testing.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure SQL Database DiskANN vector indexing
items.description:
Announcing the public preview of vector indexing using DiskANN in Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL Managed Instance and SQL database in Microsoft Fabric. DiskANN is an algorithm for efficient vector similarity search, making it ideal for product recommendations or image search applications. Designed for large-scale vector search and recommendation systems, DiskANN seamlessly integrates with the existing capabilities of Microsoft SQL query engine, enabling you to build complex, multimodal semantic search capabilities in modern applications. 

 

This release follows the general availability of the vector data type and vector functions announced this summer, giving you foundational AI capabilities right in the database engine. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure SQL Managed Instance Next-gen General Purpose service tier
items.description:
The Next‑gen General Purpose tier delivers a major performance boost while preserving the cost advantages you expect. You get more power and compute flexibility without sacrificing the simplicity of a fully managed platform as a service (PaaS) experience. 

 

You can immediately get 3 to 5 times better performance simply by upgrading from the classic General Purpose tier. For more demanding workloads, you can fine‑tune your environment using configurable IOPS and adjustable memory‑to‑vCore ratios, getting the control you need to optimize without adding unnecessary costs. 

 

With Next‑gen General Purpose, you can run heavier workloads, scale with confidence, and achieve a better price-to-performance balance—all while staying on a fully managed service. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Database for PostgreSQL storage extension support for Parquet
items.description:
Announcing that Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server now supports the Azure Storage extension with Parquet format and multiple compression options. You can seamlessly read and write Parquet files directly from your database, enabling faster data exchange with analytics and storage systems while reducing storage costs through efficient compression. With this capability, you can simplify your data pipelines, improve performance for large-scale workloads, and optimize your cloud storage usage—all without leaving your PostgreSQL environment. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Mirroring in Fabric for PostgreSQL Flexible Server
items.description:
You can now bring data together and simplify analytics using Microsoft Fabric mirroring for Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server, now generally available. Mirroring in Fabric unifies your organizational data in OneLake and supports network-isolated servers (using virtual networks or private endpoints) and highly available configurations. To enhance app integration with rich business insights, you can join data across various sources and enjoy one-click integration with Microsoft Power BI. For swift, efficient access, you can optimize your data using the Delta Lake table features. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: PostgreSQL extension for Visual Studio Code with GitHub Copilot
items.description:
Announcing that the PostgreSQL extension for Visual Studio Code is generally available. With this powerful tool, you can connect to PostgreSQL database instances, run queries, create and manage connection profiles, and take advantage of Microsoft Entra ID support, context-aware IntelliSense, syntax highlighting, and SQL formatting. Designed to boost your productivity and streamline development, the extension includes automated local database container deployments in Docker and the ability to chat with GitHub Copilot. With this extension, you can manage your PostgreSQL databases directly within your development environment, eliminating the need for context switching.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: PostgreSQL 18 with in-place upgrade on Azure Database for PostgreSQL
items.description:
You can now use PostgreSQL 18 on Azure Database for PostgreSQL. This release introduces the latest PostgreSQL innovations along with seamless in-place upgrade support, allowing you to move from earlier versions without changing your server endpoint, reconfiguring applications, or migrating data manually. You can stay current with minimal downtime and reduced operational complexity while benefiting from a fully managed service. 

 

PostgreSQL 18 delivers significant improvements in performance, scalability, and developer productivity, including asynchronous I/O (AIO) for faster queries, enhanced vacuuming, UUIDv7 support, logical replication enhancements, and virtual generated columns for flexible schema design. By adopting PostgreSQL 18 on Azure Database for PostgreSQL, you gain access to the newest community features with enterprise-grade reliability, built-in security, and high availability. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure SQL change event streaming
items.description:
You can now stream data changes in near real time from Azure SQL Database directly into Azure Event Hubs. With the public preview of change event streaming (CES), you can streamline data integration and support enhanced analytics, event-driven architectures, and the modernization of monolithic applications. 

 

By streaming operational data from SQL databases to Azure Event Hubs, you can seamlessly integrate this data into real-time dashboards, microservices, and various downstream systems, reducing the delays and complexities associated with traditional batch-based pipelines. Data is transferred from SQL only once and can be accessed by multiple consumers, minimizing polling on operational databases. Additionally, when data is available on a common message bus, it becomes more accessible for new consumers, unlocking faster innovation such as AI solution development. 

 

CES offers near real-time latency, an “at least once” message delivery guarantee, and minimal impact on source workloads.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server pg_duckdb extension
items.description:
Now you can create pg_duckdb extensions in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server, so you can accelerate analytics using DuckDB’s vectorized, columnar execution. 
 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server v6 series VMs and AMD v6 Confidential Compute
items.description:
Now you can deploy general purpose and memory-optimized v6-series Azure Virtual Machines with local NVMe storage in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server. The v6 series is available with either Intel or AMD processor options. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server anon extension
items.description:
The anon extension is now generally available in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server. This extension provides data anonymization tools. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Native Microsoft Foundry support for Azure Database for PostgreSQL
items.description:
Announcing the public preview of Microsoft Foundry support for Azure Database for PostgreSQL. The Azure PostgreSQL MCP Server is now natively integrated with Microsoft Foundry. 

 

This integration enables you to build AI agents to securely query and analyze PostgreSQL data using natural language, with support for data retrieval, vector search, schema discovery, and more. 

 

With enterprise-grade security via Microsoft Entra ID, plus support for row-level access controls, this release accelerates AI adoption across your organization. 

 

You can onboard in minutes using the Microsoft Foundry SDK or the Microsoft Agent Framework to build agents that interact with the Azure Database for PostgreSQL MCP Server. For added data security, you can also self-host the MCP Server using Azure Container Apps or Azure Functions on their own Azure subscriptions and virtual networks. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Elastic clusters on Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server
items.description:
Now you can use elastic clusters to horizontally scale Azure Database for PostgreSQL through row-based and schema-based sharding. Elastic clusters make it easy to build multitenant apps by offloading shard management and operations—such as tenant isolation, split, or online rebalancing of shards—to the service.  

 

Row-based sharding is ideal for multitenant software as a service (SaaS) deployments, as it splits tenants into rows within a cluster-distributed table, enhancing density and improving margins per tenant. Alternatively, schema-based sharding suits microservices and lift-and-shift migrations of existing applications, offering more customization of schemas for each tenant.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: 2025 REST API for Azure Database for PostgreSQL
items.description:
Announcing the general availability of the 2025 REST API for Azure Database for PostgreSQL. This release adds support for PostgreSQL 17 and 18, so you can adopt new versions without changing your automation patterns. You can also now set the default database name for elastic clusters. To improve the developer experience, we have renamed operation IDs for clearer navigation, and corrected HTTP response codes so scripts and retries behave as expected. Security guidance gets a boost with a new customer-managed key (CMK) encryption example that demonstrates automatic key version updates. Finally, the specification is easier to use with renamed files for accuracy, a reorganized structure that simplifies browsing and diffs, and enhanced local definition metadata—delivering a clearer, safer, and more capable API for your 2025 roadmaps. 

Learn more

items.title: Public Preview: Oracle to PostgreSQL migration tooling in Visual Studio Code
items.description:
Migrating from Oracle to PostgreSQL is now simpler and faster with the new Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration tooling, available directly in the Azure Database for PostgreSQL extension for Visual Studio Code. 

 

This new tool helps you seamlessly convert your Oracle schemas and application code to PostgreSQL equivalents without leaving your development environment. You can extract Oracle schema files, validate conversions in a scratch PostgreSQL database, and review AI-assisted conversion recommendations—all through a step-by-step guided wizard inside Visual Studio Code. 

 

The tool automatically identifies Oracle-specific constructs and transforms them into PostgreSQL-compatible syntax while flagging any items that require developer review. In the background, integration with Azure OpenAI Service brings intelligent code conversion to both database and application layers, reducing manual rework and accelerating migration readiness. 

 

In addition to database schema conversion, the new Application Migration capability leverages GitHub Copilot Agent Mode together with specialized Oracle-to-PostgreSQL conversion tools to modernize client application code. 

 

Whether you’re modernizing a single application or moving enterprise workloads, this tool helps you streamline end-to-end migration, ensure compatibility, and get to PostgreSQL faster. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Online migration from Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB RU to Azure DocumentDB
items.description:
Announcing the general availability of seamless, self-serve online migrations from Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB RU to Azure DocumentDB—directly from the Azure portal. With this release, your organization can modernize its MongoDB workloads with zero downtime, no cost, and minimal operational overhead. 

 

The migration engine reads natively from Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB RU and writes to Azure DocumentDB, ensuring compatibility and performance across diverse workloads. It supports both offline and online migrations. Microsoft Entra ID integration and partition-level read optimization are already available. 

 

You can start using this capability today to accelerate the journey to Azure DocumentDB—unlocking advanced features, improved performance, and a future-ready architecture. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Online and offline migrations in Azure DocumentDB Migration extension
items.description:
You can now migrate MongoDB workloads to Azure DocumentDB using the new Azure DocumentDB Migration extension for Visual Studio Code—now available in public preview. This seamless, zero-cost migration supports both online and offline modes, simplifying and accelerating your modernization journey. 

 

The migration jobs run entirely on Azure–managed resources, maintained by the Azure Cosmos DB team, so you don’t need to install or manage any infrastructure. You can initiate and monitor migrations without staying connected throughout the process, making it ideal for secure and large-scale scenarios. The extension also supports private endpoint-enabled targets, ensuring enterprise-grade security and compliance. 

 

Whether you're migrating from self-hosted MongoDB, MongoDB Atlas, or other compatible sources, this extension provides a unified, intuitive experience directly within Visual Studio Code. You benefit from improved performance, reduced operational overhead, and a streamlined path to Azure DocumentDB—all without incurring additional migration costs. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Dynamic data masking with Azure Cosmos DB
items.description:
You can now help protect sensitive data from unauthorized access using dynamic data masking (DDM), a server-side, policy-based security feature in Azure Cosmos DB. DDM dynamically masks data for non-privileged users, ensuring that sensitive information is redacted in real time before being presented to applications, while the original data remains unchanged in the database. 

 

DDM can help your organization meet security, compliance, and regulatory requirements by limiting exposure of sensitive data, including personally identifiable information (PII) and protected health information (PHI). 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure DocumentDB - an open-source, MongoDB-compatible document database service for hybrid and multicloud
items.description:
Microsoft is announcing the general availability of Azure DocumentDB, a fully managed document database service built on the open-source, MongoDB-compatible DocumentDB, now governed by the Linux Foundation. Formerly known as Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB (vCore), Azure DocumentDB gives you the power of open source with the performance, security, and scale of Azure. 

  

What you gain: 

  • Freedom and flexibility. Build once and deploy anywhere with a consistent open-source MongoDB-compatible database that runs across hybrid and multi-cloud environments. 

  • AI-ready innovation. Use built-in vector and hybrid search to power retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), copilots, and other intelligent applications. 

  • Elastic performance. Get instant autoscale and independent compute and storage scaling—so you pay only for what you use. 

  • Enterprise-grade reliability and security. Protect your data with Microsoft Entra ID authentication, customer-managed keys, and 35-day backups at no additional cost, backed by 99.999% uptime full-stack service-level agreements and around-the-clock Azure support. 

 

With Azure DocumentDB, you can modernize your MongoDB workloads, build AI-driven apps faster, and scale globally on an open, flexible, and enterprise-ready foundation. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Cosmos DB fleet pools
items.description:
Now you can more easily operate your Azure Cosmos DB accounts at scale. Azure Cosmos DB fleet pools give you new capabilities when building multitenant software as a service (SaaS) applications. 

 

You can simplify capacity management by creating a pool of throughput (RU/s) that can be shared by accounts in the fleet. You get all the security and performance isolation benefits of creating one Azure Cosmos DB account to represent a tenant or end customer, while also efficiently sharing RU/s resources across tenants to avoid overprovisioning at the per-tenant level. Throughput pooling is now generally available. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Cosmos DB Fleet Analytics
items.description:
You can now unify insights across your entire Azure Cosmos DB footprint using Azure Cosmos DB Fleet Analytics, available in public preview. Fleet Analytics helps you manage data across multiple accounts, subscriptions, and workloads, providing large-scale, cross-account analytics for Azure Cosmos DB.  

 

You can analyze performance, usage, and billing trends in one place, so you can manage growth, optimize efficiency, and ensure consistency across your fleet. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Priority-based execution in Azure Cosmos DB
items.description:
You can now enable priority-based execution in Azure Cosmos DB to ensure that high-priority requests are favored during periods of contention. The system will throttle low-priority requests first, allowing high-priority operations to proceed on a best-effort basis. 

 

Using the Azure Cosmos DB SDK, you can assign each request a priority level (high or low). Low priority requests are retried according to the configured retry policy, helping maintain responsiveness for critical workloads. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Index Advisor for Azure DocumentDB
items.description:
Integrated into the DocumentDB for VS Code extension, the Index Advisor enables you to view and debug database performance. It uses natural language to recommend optimal indexing and best practices for your MongoDB workloads.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Cosmos DB in Microsoft Fabric
items.description:
Now generally available, Cosmos DB in Fabric enables you to build operational and analytical workloads in Microsoft Fabric. You can use the AI-features in Azure Cosmos DB plus the innovations in Fabric to run SQL queries over JSON data and build real-time intelligence over transactional data. You can also use Azure Cosmos DB as a lightning fast serving layer for Microsoft Power BI, using Spark for reverse extract, transform, load (ETL)—all without having to stitch together separate services.  

 

Cosmos DB in Fabric includes many new features, such as user-defined functions for seamlessly connecting to your Cosmos DB artifacts. With support for continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD), you can manage development, test, and production pipelines. This release also supports Cosmos DB autoscaling for elasticity when you need it, and vector and full-text indexing and search are enabled by default to support your AI-enabled workloads. We are also announcing Fabric CMK support in Preview. This release marks a major step toward making operational data readily accessible across the Fabric ecosystem. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Cosmos DB Mirroring in Microsoft Fabric
items.description:
Now generally available, Azure Cosmos DB Mirroring in Fabric enables you to seamlessly integrate your existing operational workloads with the analytical capabilities of Microsoft Fabric. You can take advantage of the innovations in Fabric, running SQL queries over JSON data and building real-time intelligence over your existing transactional data. You can integrate your data with the Microsoft Fabric ecosystem of services and work with Copilot-assisted Microsoft Power BI—all without having to stitch together separate services.  

 

With Azure Cosmos DB Mirroring in Fabric, you can select the containers to mirror into Fabric, giving you complete control over the data used for analytics. You get the best of both worlds—the latency and availability of Azure Cosmos DB and the array of analytical capabilities in Microsoft Fabric. This release makes it even easier to make your existing operational data accessible across the Fabric ecosystem. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Cosmos DB for Visual Studio Code
items.description:
Developers today are building more intelligent, connected, and autonomous applications than ever before. From personalized chatbots and copilots to dynamic content engines and decision systems, data is the foundation of these agentic experiences. 

 
Azure Cosmos DB already plays a central role in powering these workloads, offering globally distributed, low-latency, highly scalable data services with flexible API support. However, developers told us they wanted a way to interact with their Cosmos DB data directly from Visual Studio Code (VS Code), where they already spend most of their time writing, debugging, and testing code. 
 
With this release, we’re delivering exactly that—a unified, fast, and developer-first experience for working with Azure Cosmos DB data without leaving your coding environment. 
 
Now generally available, Azure Cosmos DB for VS Code comes with significant updates focused on usability, stability, and performance. It incorporates months of feedback from preview users, who helped shape this extension into the powerful tool it is today. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Float16 data type for vector indexes in Azure Cosmos DB
items.description:
Azure Cosmos DB now supports float 16 data types for vector indexes. With this update, you can store and query vectors using half-precision floating-point numbers. Using float16 cuts storage usage in half compared to float32, while maintaining high retrieval accuracy for most AI workloads. 

 

Float16 can be especially useful for large-scale scenarios when you need to store many vector embeddings. By reducing vector size, you can lower indexing and storage costs, making it easier to scale semantic search and AI agent memory retrieval. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Vector indexing performance improvements in Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL
items.description:
This release gives you faster vector inserts and index builds in Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL, helping you reduce end-to-end ingestion and indexing times for large AI workloads. This improvement is powered by algorithmic enhancements to our vector indexing engine. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Fuzzy search in Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL full-text search
items.description:
Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL now supports fuzzy search in full-text search. With fuzzy search, you can deliver typo-tolerant, error-resilient search experiences directly within Azure Cosmos DB, helping your users find the right results even when queries or the data itself contain errors. This feature improves the quality and usability of search-driven applications, making them feel more natural and forgiving for end users. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Cosmos DB MCP ToolKit for Microsoft Foundry Agent Service
items.description:
Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL now offers an MCP Toolkit that can be used with Microsoft Foundry Agent Service, available today in public preview. 

 

This new integration allows you to connect Microsoft Foundry Agents directly to data in Azure Cosmos DB. By deploying the Azure Cosmos DB MCP Toolkit Server in your Azure environment, you can enable your agents to perform secure data operations and run semantic searches within Azure Cosmos DB. 

 

The toolkit includes multiple ready-to-use tools that simplify setup and configuration, helping your agents discover data and retrieve the right information for reasoning and task execution. You can now build data-aware agents that respond to user requests with information drawn from live operational data. The integration in Microsoft Foundry Agents Service makes it easy to connect to the MCP server and get started. 

 

With vector search, full-text search, and high-performance NoSQL capabilities built into Azure Cosmos DB, your AI solutions can deliver faster and more contextually relevant results at a global scale.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Support for Italian and Portuguese in Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL full-text search
items.description:
Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL now supports Italian and Portuguese languages in full-text search, available today in public preview. This update adds to the list of supported languages, enabling you to build rich, language-aware search experiences that understand the linguistic nuances of Italian and Portuguese text. 

 

You can more easily create multilingual applications that deliver a natural and localized search experience for users across Europe and Latin America. Whether you’re building e-commerce catalogs, customer knowledge bases, or AI-powered chat and discovery tools, you can now seamlessly search across Italian and Portuguese content without needing to preprocess or translate data. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: SQL database in Microsoft Fabric
items.description:
SQL database in Fabric is now generally available. Built on the trusted SQL Server and Azure SQL Database engine, this fully SaaS-native solution empowers developers and data professionals to unify operational and analytical workloads with speed, security, and AI-powered capabilities. Key highlights include fast provisioning, Copilot-powered management, autonomous scaling, enterprise-grade security (with Customer Managed Keys and SQL Auditing), and native support for AI scenarios like semantic search and RAG.
Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Standard V2 NAT Gateway and StandardV2 Public IPs
items.description:
StandardV2 SKU NAT Gateway is now in public preview, delivering next-generation capabilities for scalable and resilient outbound connectivity. 

New offerings: 

  • Zone-Redundancy: Built for high availability in availability zone supported regions. Traffic survives single-zone failures with no extra configurations required. 

  • Enhanced performance: Supports up to 100 Gbps of throughput and 10 million packets per second, double the Standard SKU capacity. 

  • Dual-stack support: Supports up to 16 IPv6 and 16 IPv4 public IP addresses for future ready connectivity. 

  • Traffic insights with Flow logs: Provides IP-level traffic insights for troubleshooting and verifying compliance with organizational policies and requirements. 

  • StandardV2 Public IPs: StandardV2 NAT Gateway requires StandardV2 IPs; Standard SKU IPs are not supported. 

Pricing and availability: 

  • Same price as the Standard SKU NAT Gateway. 

  • Available in select regions, with broader rollout planned. 

  • Deploy through CLI, Powershell, Bicep and ARM. Portal support coming soon.  

Learn more: 

  • StandardV2 NAT Gateway  

  • StandardV2 Public IPs

items.title: Public Preview: Confidential computing in Azure Container Apps
items.description:
Confidential computing support in Azure Container Apps is now in public preview. This release brings hardware-based Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) to your containerized workloads. Azure already provides encryption of data at rest and in transit, and confidential computing provides an additional layer of protection for data in use by encrypting data in memory and processing it only after the cloud environment is verified. This helps customers prevent unauthorized access to data in use, even from the cloud operator, and is beneficial for organizations that require further protection for sensitive data and applications.  

Confidential computing is accessible through workload profiles in Azure Container Apps, and the public preview is limited to select regions. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Container Apps serverless GPUs in additional regions
items.description:
To meet growing demand for GPU-powered workloads, Azure Container Apps serverless GPUs are now generally available in additional regions. This expansion enables developers to run AI inference, model training, and GPU-accelerated workloads with the simplicity of a serverless experience.   

Newly Available Regions:   

  • Americas: East US, West US 2, South Central US, North Central US, Brazil South   
  • Asia: Japan East, Southeast Asia, Central India, South India   
  • Europe: France Central, Italy North   

Benefits of serverless GPUs:   

  • Scale-to zero GPUs: Support for automatic serverless scaling of NVIDIA A100 and NVIDIA T4 GPUs.   
  • Per-second billing: Pay only for the GPU compute you use.   
  • Built-in data governance: Your data never leaves the container boundary.   

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Container Apps introduces flexible workload profile
items.description:
Flexible workload profile represents a new option that blends the simplicity of consumption with many of the performance and control characteristics of dedicated workload profiles. This offers the same easy-to-understand, pay-per-use serverless model as Consumption, while adding features like planned maintenance windows, dedicated networking support, and access to larger replica sizes for demanding applications. Running in a single-tenant compute pool, this flexible workload profile provides improved predictability and isolation without adding operational complexity. This new profile is designed for customers who want the convenience of serverless scaling with greater control over performance and environment stability. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Container Apps adds support for agentic Docker Compose
items.description:
Azure Container Apps is bringing the familiar developer workflow of Docker Compose directly to Azure Container Apps. As one of the most widely adopted tools among developers, Docker Compose simplifies defining and running multi-container applications, and this new integration extends that ease of use to production environments. With native support in Azure Container Apps, developers can now move seamlessly from local development to cloud deployment without changing their tooling or workflow. When combined with serverless GPU support, agentic Docker Compose enables rapid iteration and scalable execution of AI-powered agents and applications. With this update, customers can now experience a developer-first platform for modern AI workloads, unifying the inner-loop and outer-loop experience into a single, consistent environment.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Functions enables OpenTelemetry support
items.description:
Azure Functions now supports OpenTelemetry in general availability (GA), enabling developers to export logs, traces, and metrics using open standards. This release builds on the public preview and delivers a production-ready observability experience for serverless applications. 

 

With this GA release, Azure Functions delivers: 

  • Unified observability – Standardize logs, traces, and metrics across your serverless workloads. 
  • Vendor-neutral telemetry – Integrate with Azure Monitor or any OpenTelemetry-compliant backend. 
  • Broad language support – Works with .NET (isolated), Java, JavaScript, Python, PowerShell, and TypeScript. 

 

Start using OpenTelemetry in Azure Functions today and bring modern, standards-based observability to your apps. View the documentation for step-by-step guidance on enabling OpenTelemetry and configuring exporters for your preferred backend.

items.title: Announcing: Resources for migrating to Azure Functions Flex Consumption
items.description:
Azure Functions Flex Consumption is now the recommended hosting plan for serverless workloads requiring advanced scaling, networking, and cost optimization. To support customers migrating from the Azure Functions Consumption plan or from AWS Lambda, Microsoft has published comprehensive migration guides and tooling:


  • Azure Functions Consumption to Flex Consumption: The new documentation provides step-by-step instructions for moving your Azure Functions apps from the Consumption plan to Flex Consumption. This includes guidance on updating your infrastructure as code (ARM/Bicep), configuration changes, and leveraging new AZ CLI commands to automate the migration process.

  • AWS Lambda to Azure Functions Flex Consumption: For customers migrating from AWS Lambda, this guide covers mapping Lambda concepts to Azure Functions, code porting strategies, and best practices for deploying to Azure Functions Flex Consumption. This includes instructions for using GitHub Copilot in VS Code for help with code refactoring, manual refactoring for specific changes, or other migration aids.


These resources are designed to minimize downtime and ensure a smooth transition, enabling customers to take advantage of Flex Consumption’s improved scaling, networking, and cost controls.

Learn more:

  • Migrate Consumption plan apps to the Flex Consumption plan 
  • Migrate AWS Lambda workloads to Azure Functions

items.title: Public Preview: Self-hosted remote MCP servers on Azure Functions
items.description:
We are introducing a new capability that allows you to host remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers built with the MCP SDKs on Functions. Some key benefits of hosting on the Functions platform include:  

  • Built-in server authentication 
  • Automatic and bursty scaling  
  • Pay-per-use 
Additionally, if you’ve already built your MCP server, you don’t need to make any code changes to host on Azure Functions.   

Currently in public preview, the new capability supports remote hosting of servers built with the Python, TypeScript, C#, and Java MCP SDKs on the Flex Consumption plan. Servers must be stateless and use the streamable-http transport.  

Learn more:
  • Documentation
  • Get started
  • Samples

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Functions durable task scheduler Dedicated SKU (GA) & Consumption SKU (Public Preview)
items.description:
Earlier this year, we introduced Azure Functions durable task scheduler, an orchestration engine designed for complex workflows and intelligent agents. It automatically checkpoints progress and protects your orchestration state, enabling resilient and reliable execution.  

Azure Functions durable task scheduler is now generally available with the Dedicated SKU, and the Consumption SKU is entering public preview.  

These offerings provide advanced orchestration capabilities for cloud-native and agentic applications, providing predictable pricing for steady workloads with the Dedicated SKU and flexible, pay-as-you-go billing for dynamic, variable workloads with the Consumption SKU. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool trigger for Azure Functions
items.description:
Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a way for apps to provide capabilities and context to a large language model. A key feature of MCP is the ability to define tools that AI agents can leverage to accomplish whatever tasks they’ve been given. MCP servers can be run locally, but remote MCP servers are important for sharing tools that work at cloud scale. 

The Azure Functions MCP tool trigger is now generally available, allowing you to build tools using remote MCP with Azure Functions. Azure Functions lets you author focused, event-driven logic that scales automatically in response to demand. You just write code reflecting unique requirements of your tools, and Functions will take care of the rest. 


Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure DocumentDB high-performance storage
items.description:
Now you can run bigger, faster workloads on fewer nodes using high-performance storage for Azure DocumentDB. This update delivers up to 64 TiB capacity, 80,000 IOPS, and 1,200 MB/s throughput per physical shard (node). Storage IOPS and throughput on Azure DocumentDB clusters with high-performance storage are always optimized by default—configured using the maximum values permitted by the selected compute and storage combination.

 
This update provides the headroom required for I/O-intensive applications and very large datasets, helping you to consolidate data that previously needed many shards and to maintain low latency at peak traffic. Real-time analytics, personalization, and high-volume commerce scenarios benefit from predictable throughput and consistent performance as you scale.
 
To get started, you can create a cluster with high-performance storage in the Azure portal, then benchmark your workload to right-size shards and compute for your targets.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Application Gateway for Containers Istio Service Mesh integration
items.description:
Application Gateway for Containers now supports integration with Istio service mesh through an optional service mesh extension. This feature simplifies secure north-south communication between external clients and services within the service mesh. 

  • Single solution: Load balance traffic to services both inside and outside the mesh through one ingress gateway.  
  • Reduced operational overhead: Eliminate configuration bloat by automating repetitive mutual authentication definitions.  
  • Certificate trust and rotation: Managed certificate trust and rotation to maintain secure authentication with the service mesh.  

Learn more: 

  • Application Gateway for Containers + Istio service mesh 
  • Application Gateway for Containers Overview

items.title: Generally Available: Application Gateway for Containers – Slow start
items.description:
Slow start is now generally available as a load balancing algorithm in Application Gateway for Containers. This feature improves stability and performance during backend scale-up by gradually increasing traffic to new pods over a configurable time window. 

Algorithm benefits: 

  • Smooth scale-up: Avoid sudden traffic spikes that can cause cold-start delays or failures. 
  • Improved reliability: Ensure new pods are ready before handling peak load. 
  • Predictable performance: Maintain consistent response times during scaling events and rolling updates. 

Learn more: 

  • Load Balancing Strategies with Application Gateway for Containers 
  • Application Gateway for Containers Overview

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Functions support for Java 25
items.description:
You can now develop functions using Java 25 locally and deploy them to Azure Functions on Windows and Linux. 

 

Upgrade your apps to Java 25 to take advantage of enhanced security, a longer support window, and continued compatibility with the Azure Functions runtime and developer tools. 

 

Learn more: 

  • Java support in Azure Functions 
  • Upgrade your app to Java 25

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Functions support for Node.js 24
items.description:
You can now develop functions using Node.js 24 locally and deploy them to Azure Functions on Windows and Linux.  

 

Note: Node.js 24 does not support 32-bit systems on Windows. To ensure compatibility, new Windows Function Apps for Node.js 24 now default to 64-bit. Please make sure your app is deployed using 64-bit. 

 

Upgrade your apps to Node.js 24 to take advantage of enhanced security, a longer support window, and continued compatibility with the Azure Functions runtime and developer tools. 

 

Learn more: 

  • Updates in the latest Node.js version 

  • Upgrade your app to Node.js 24 

  • Node.js support in Azure Functions

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Virtual Network Manager address overlap prevention in mesh
items.description:
Azure Virtual Network Manager address space overlap prevention in mesh is now generally available, bringing enhanced reliability and governance to multi-virtual network environments. 

Unintended address overlap within mesh can lead to dropped traffic. This feature introduces a built-in validation mechanism to proactively detect and prevent such conflicts. 

With this capability: 

  • When adding a virtual network to a mesh, Azure Virtual Network Manager automatically verifies that the new virtual network’s address space does not overlap with existing members. 
  • When updating an existing virtual network’s address space or adding a new peering, Azure Virtual Network Manager ensures the operation will not introduce an overlap. 

Any address change triggers an update to Azure Virtual Network Manager, ensuring real-time validation and consistent routing integrity across large-scale environments. 

This GA release empowers customers to maintain end-to-end network reliability, prevent configuration-induced outages, and uphold governance standards across distributed Azure deployments. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Cross region pool association support for Azure Virtual Network Manager IP address management
items.description:
Managing IP address spaces across multiple regions can be complex and error-prone.  

With this new capability, you can now associate a single IPAM pool with virtual networks in multiple regions, simplifying governance and ensuring consistent CIDR allocation globally.  

Key benefits include: 

  • Simplified management: Consolidate address planning into one multi-region pool instead of per-region pools. 
  • Consistent governance: Enforce CIDR policies across regions with flexible region restrictions. 
  • Backward compatibility: Existing single-region pools continue to work seamlessly. 

This enhancement enables global-scale deployments while reducing operational overhead and maintaining precise control of address allocation across your Azure footprint.  

This preview feature is available in select regions. To get started, please refer to the documentation for guidance on enabling this preview feature.

items.title: Public Preview: Add durability to AI agents in Azure Functions using Microsoft Agent Framework
items.description:
You can now build and host reliable production-grade AI agents using the durable extension for Microsoft Agent Framework. This integration combines the Microsoft Agent Framework with Azure Functions’ durable capabilities, delivering proven orchestration and resilience for serverless AI agent hosting. You gain automatic session management, built-in HTTP endpoints, and elastic scaling from zero to thousands of instances—all with pay-per-use pricing and automated infrastructure management. 

 

Key capabilities include: 

  • Stateful agent sessions: Maintain persistent conversation history across distributed instances with automatic failover for uninterrupted operation. 
  • Durable tool calls: Checkpoint progress during long-running tool invocations, extending beyond typical timeout limits. 
  • Deterministic multi-agent orchestration: Coordinate specialized agents through predictable, code-driven workflows that survive failures and restarts. 
  • Human-in-the-loop workflows: Pause orchestrations for days or weeks awaiting human approval at zero compute cost, then resume seamlessly. 
  • Built-in observability: Access deep insights via the durable task scheduler dashboard with execution replay, conversation history, and integrated performance metrics. 

The extension supports both C# and Python, enabling developers to deploy AI agents confidently on Azure Functions with enterprise-grade durability and scalability.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: AKS Automatic managed system node pools
items.description:
Provisioning and maintaining system node pools in AKS requires ongoing effort to ensure proper scaling, patching, and availability, tasks that can divert resources from application development and delivery.

Managed system node pools in AKS Automatic removes this operational burden by providing a fully managed infrastructure layer that handles system components without customer intervention. This means teams no longer need to maintain infrastructure for system workloads, allowing them to focus entirely on deploying and scaling applications. By isolating system workloads from customer applications, AKS Automatic improves reliability and ensures consistent performance backed by SLAs. The result is faster time to value, reduced infrastructure overhead, and a simplified path to Kubernetes adoption.
Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: AKS Automatic pod readiness SLA
items.description:
Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) Automatic clusters now come with a pod readiness SLA, guaranteeing that eligible pods meet readiness criteria within five minutes at the 99.9th percentile. This empowers customers to confidently deploy mission critical workloads, knowing that their infrastructure is reliable and comes with financial backing.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Windows Server 2025 on AKS
items.description:
Organizations running Windows-based workloads on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) face increasing pressure to modernize as support timelines for older Windows Server versions approach retirement. To help customers prepare, AKS now offers preview support for Windows Server 2025, bringing significant improvements over Windows Server 2022.  

 

Windows Server 2025 provides many improvements as compared to Windows Server 2022:  

  • Stable ABI: Allows you to run Windows Server 2022 containers on Windows Server 2025 
  • New defaults: Generation 2 VM, containerd 2.0, FIPS enablement 
  • Improved Nano server flexibility and added functionality: For example, Nano server now contains support for 32-bit apps via a FoD 
  • Improved GPU support: CUDA workloads can now run in a container 

With upcoming retirements for Windows Server 2019 on March 1, 2026 and Windows Server 2022 on March 15, 2027, we recommend testing out the new Windows Server version to prepare for your migration. When migrating to Windows Server 2025, you’ll need to recreate your node pools with the new OS and migrate existing workloads. 
Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Kubernetes Fleet Manager for Arc-enabled clusters
items.description:
Managing Kubernetes clusters across hybrid and multi-cloud environments can be complex and fragmented. To simplify this, Azure Kubernetes Fleet Manager now supports Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes, enabling organizations to seamlessly manage any CNCF-compliant Kubernetes distribution, regardless of where it’s running.


By Arc-enabling clusters and joining them as Fleet Manager member clusters, users gain centralized visibility into cluster health. Fleet Manager also empowers cluster administrators and application teams with intelligent workload placement, making it easier to deploy configurations and applications consistently across environments. 

This enhancement helps reduce operational overhead, improves deployment agility, and ensures consistent governance across distributed Kubernetes infrastructure.
Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Managed namespaces on AKS
items.description:
Managing namespace configurations across AKS clusters has traditionally required manual setup and ongoing maintenance, creating complexity and potential for misconfiguration. With the general availability of Managed Namespaces, AKS now enables users to easily deploy preconfigured namespaces with built-in lifecycle management. 

This feature simplifies the process of applying consistent controls across clusters, including ingress/egress network policies, RBAC, and resource limits/requests. By offloading namespace lifecycle management to Azure, teams can accelerate deployment, improve governance, and reduce operational overhead.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Pod sandboxing on AKS
items.description:
Running containerized workloads in shared environments can raise concerns around security and workload isolation. To address this, AKS now supports pod sandboxing, enabling customers to run containers in per-workload pod VMs. Each pod VM is isolated from others and from the host, providing a strong compute isolation boundary. 

This feature enhances workload security by reducing the risk of cross-pod interference and host-level vulnerabilities, making it ideal for multi-tenant scenarios or sensitive applications.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Kubernetes Service desktop
items.description:
AKS desktop delivers a modern, application-centric experience for deploying and managing workloads on Azure Kubernetes Service. Built on supported AKS features, best practices, and the open-source Headlamp project, it offers a guided, self-service interface that simplifies Kubernetes operations while preserving control. 


Designed to integrate with existing environments and tools, AKS desktop enables seamless team collaboration through role-based access control (RBAC), helping teams move faster and stay aligned.


Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Container Registry Repository Permissions with Attribute-based Access Control (ABAC)
items.description:
Organizations operating Azure Container Registries (ACR) require least-privilege permissions over which Microsoft Entra identities can publish or consume container images. With ACR repository permissions using attribute-based access control (ABAC), administrators can now grant granular repository and namespace-level permissions. This enables secure container registry operations by ensuring that CI/CD pipelines and Kubernetes workloads can only perform image push, pull, or delete operations on authorized repositories. 

 

ABAC is available for both new and existing ACR registries, across all SKUs, in all regions.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: ExpressRoute Scalable Gateway
items.description:
ExpressRoute Scalable Gateway (ErGwScale) is our next-generation offering that brings flexibility, performance, and operational simplicity to Virtual Network Gateway deployments. With this release, you can dynamically scale gateway infrastructure to meet real-time traffic demands. 

What’s new 

  • Dynamic scaling: Deploy ErGwScale to achieve up to 40 Gbps of connectivity for virtual machines and private endpoints within your virtual network. 
  • Auto scaling: Configure minimum and maximum scale units, and Azure automatically adjusts capacity based on bandwidth and flow demand—delivering efficiency and eliminating manual tuning. 
  • Fixed scale option: For predictable workloads, set a steady scale to maintain consistent bandwidth for stable traffic patterns. 
  • FastPath + gateway coexistence: ErGwScale complements FastPath for scenarios where FastPath isn’t supported—such as high-bandwidth or complex routing cases—ensuring seamless performance. 

This offering introduces elastic scaling, zero-downtime upgrades, and enterprise-grade reliability, making it ideal for hybrid connectivity and demanding workloads. 

 Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure VNet Flow Log - Filtering
items.description:
VNet Flow Log captures IP traffic flowing through VNets, Subnets, & NICs for monitoring, troubleshooting, network optimization, security, and compliance needs. 

This release introduces advanced filtering capabilities in VNet Flow Logs, empowering users with unprecedented granular control over network traffic logging. With support for nine distinct criteria including IP addresses, ports, protocols, encryption state, allowed/denied actions, flow states, and traffic directions.  

This empowers organization to surgically capture only the traffic that truly matters most to their operations. This flexibility enables selective recording of intra/inter-VNet traffic, CIDR-based flows, inbound/outbound traffic or traffic flowing through specific ports and much more all through intuitive logical operations of AND and OR.  By prioritizing critical flows and tailoring monitoring to user preferences, organizations gain faster, more actionable insights while maintaining robust network visibility 

This release aids significant operational efficiencies by dramatically reducing log volume and noise. By targeting only relevant traffic logs, organizations can streamline troubleshooting, minimize data processing overhead, and lower total cost of ownership (TCO) through reduced storage requirements. The simplified log management not only preserves essential visibility but also ensures compliance and security monitoring remain uncompromised. environments. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Network Watcher Topology – AKS Visualization
items.description:
Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) visualization in Network Watcher Topology (Public Preview) delivers end-to-end visibility of AKS clusters directly within the Azure networking experience. Customers can now explore their Kubernetes environments, including the control plane, node pools, and connected Azure resources, through an intuitive, interactive topology view. 

With this release, organizations can visualize AKS clusters as part of their broader network topology, closing the gap between Kubernetes workloads and Azure infrastructure. Users can trace dependencies, understand traffic paths, and identify connectivity issues - all within a single unified map. 

This capability simplifies troubleshooting and performance analysis by visually mapping relationships between pods, services, load balancers, and underlying VNets or subnets. It enables teams to collaboratively diagnose issues and maintain consistent visibility across layers. 

Integrating AKS visualization into Network Watcher Topology improves operational efficiency by reducing investigation time, minimizing tool switching, and providing actionable insights at a glance. It bridges the visibility gap between infrastructure and containerized workloads, empowering teams to maintain reliable, secure, and optimized AKS deployments. 

With AKS visualization in Topology, customers gain a unified, Azure-native view of their network landscape, ensuring awareness from the network edge to the container.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Network Watcher – Agentless Connection Troubleshoot
items.description:
Agentless Connection Troubleshoot (public preview) introduces a faster, simpler, and fully agentless way to diagnose network connectivity issues across Azure resources. Previously, running connectivity checks required installing the Network Watcher Extension on virtual machines, adding setup overhead and potential deployment delays. With this release, customers can now perform end-to-end connectivity tests without deploying any agents or extensions, reducing friction and improving reliability. 

With Agentless Connection Troubleshoot, users can instantly validate reachability, latency, and packet loss between Azure resources directly from the Azure portal, CLI, or API, with no dependency on VM configuration. This enables faster diagnostics while maintaining the same level of accuracy and depth as extension-based checks. 

This enhancement simplifies network troubleshooting by removing manual setup steps and potential extension failures, ensuring consistent results across environments. It also strengthens security posture by reducing in-guest dependencies and operational overhead. 

By making Connection Troubleshoot completely agentless, Azure empowers users to detect, triage, and resolve connectivity issues faster while improving operational efficiency and scalability. Customers can now run comprehensive connectivity tests instantly, enabling frictionless, reliable, and secure network diagnostics across their Azure workloads. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Advanced sampling and richer data collection in Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Distro
items.description:
Azure continues to embrace open standards by adding new capabilities to the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Distro that powers Azure Monitor Application Insights. 

New Capabilities:

  • Rate-limited sampling and trace-based log sampling: New sampling options in the Distro provide an alternative to the existing fixed-rate (percentage-based) sampler.
