Rate-limited sampling helps you control data ingestion by capping the number of traces collected per second and trace-based log sampling drops any logs correlated with sampled out traces, providing predictable cost management while maintaining reliable observability. Learn More.
  • Performance Counters: Azure Monitor’s OpenTelemetry Distro now automatically collects system and process metrics, known as performance counters, that power key Application Insights experiences. These metrics provide deeper visibility into application performance and help you quickly diagnose and resolve performance issues. Learn More.
  • New Telemetry Attributes: We’ve worked with the OpenTelemetry community to add Synthetic Source, Device IP Address, and Device OS/Browser to the semantic model. By bringing these fields into the official OpenTelemetry data model and Azure Monitor Distro, you can now seamlessly filter by synthetic traffic indicators, enrich client-source context, and segment telemetry by platform—making monitoring smarter, investigations faster, and insights more actionable. Learn More.

items.title: Public Preview: New integration and extensibility capabilities to Azure SRE Agent
items.description:
Azure SRE Agent is an AI-driven solution that unifies operational workflows into a single, prompt-based automation layer—eliminating complexity and reducing overhead for modern cloud operations. Unlike traditional, static automation solutions, SRE Agent leverages AI and natural-language prompts to transform unstructured domain knowledge into dynamic, context-aware automation at scale. What's new:

No-Code Automation

Empower teams to tailor operational processes to their unique environments without engineering overhead—accelerating adoption and reducing time-to-value.

Event-Driven Triggers

Enable proactive checks and instant incident response to minimize downtime and protect revenue streams.

Expanded Observability

Gain deeper visibility across Azure and third-party sources to speed troubleshooting and root cause analysis.

Orchestration Across MCP-Compatible Tools

Integrate any MCP-compatible solution for end-to-end process automation, ensuring seamless workflows across your ecosystem.

Adaptive Memory System

SRE Agent learns from every interaction to continuously improve incident handling and reduce operational toil—helping organizations achieve higher reliability at lower cost.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: NCv6 Virtual Machines
items.description:
We are announcing the public preview of NCv6 RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition Virtual Machines, as the next enhancement of NC Series VMs available on Azure.

Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 BSE GPUs are designed to accelerate a wide array of workloads including video streaming, graphics rendering, product design, digital twins, and AI development. The NCv6 VM family will be available in three categories to best suit your workload needs:  

  • Compute optimized - NClds_RTXPRO6000BSE_v6 - designed for AI and LLM inferencing workloads 
  • Memory optimized - NCmds_RTXPRO6000BSE_v6 - tailored for visualization and graphics workloads 
  • General purpose - NCds_RTXPRO6000BSE_v6 - category ideal for VDI and general-purpose AI workloads. 

For workloads running NCv6, customer experience will be the same as other NC and NV Series VMs such as T4, A100, and H100, with all currently supported workloads from those SKUs also supported on NCv6. Additionally, NCv6 VM SKUs will come with integrated NVIDIA vGPU licenses and support Multi Instance GPU (MIG), enabling greater flexibility and efficiency for a variety of use cases. 

Sign up for the public preview. 

Learn more.

items.title: Private Preview: Azure Boost remote storage throughput and network bandwidth enhancements
items.description:
Remote storage throughput and network bandwidth performance enhancements for the latest Azure Boost architecture are now in preview. 

Azure Boost is a Microsoft Azure system that offloads virtualization tasks—such as networking, storage, and host management—from the hypervisor and host OS to purpose-built hardware and software, freeing CPU resources for customer workloads while enhancing security through physical isolation and hardware root of trust. By reducing maintenance impact and improving scalability, Azure Boost enables faster, more secure, and highly efficient cloud operations for demanding workloads.  

Performance enhancements of this latest architecture include up to 20 GBps remote storage throughput, up to 1 M remote storage IOPS, and up to 400 Gbps network bandwidth. These enhancements will be available beginning with the D/E/Fsv7 Intel “Granite Rapids” VMs (in preview). Other new VMs will also begin using this architecture and will provide similar performance capabilities. 

You can learn more about these new Azure Boost performance enhancements by reading the blog. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Microsoft HTTP DDoS Ruleset 1.0 on Application Gateway WAF v2
items.description:
Announcing the public preview of the HTTP DDoS Ruleset for Application Gateway WAF v2. 

HTTP-layer DDoS attacks remain a leading cause of application downtime, and traditional static controls often fall short against evolving botnets. The new HTTP DDoS Ruleset for Azure WAF introduces automated, adaptive Layer 7 protection that learns, detects, and defends with minimal configuration. Once assigned, the ruleset continuously baselines normal traffic for each Application Gateway and, when attack surges are detected, selectively blocks offending clients with no emergency tuning required. 

The HTTP DDoS Ruleset features: 

  • Automated learning of traffic baselines at both the gateway and per-IP level. 
  • Dynamic thresholds and sensitivity settings to balance protection and user experience. 
  • Two core rules: one for high-rate client anomalies and one for suspected bots, leveraging Microsoft Threat Intelligence. 

Currently, portal access for this feature is via the preview portal.  

Learn more.

items.title: Private Preview: Azure Boost confidential device
items.description:
The Azure Boost confidential device feature is now in preview. 

Azure Boost is a Microsoft Azure system that offloads virtualization tasks—such as networking, storage, and host management—from the hypervisor and host OS to purpose-built hardware and software, freeing CPU resources for customer workloads while enhancing security through physical isolation and hardware root of trust. By reducing maintenance impact and improving scalability, Azure Boost enables faster, more secure, and highly efficient cloud operations for demanding workloads. 

The Azure Boost confidential device feature is designed specifically for upcoming versions of Azure confidential VMs and will allow the confidential computing trust boundary of these VMs to be extended into the Azure Boost card using the PCIe TDISP standard. This standard supports hardware-based attestation of the Azure Boost card and hardware-based encryption of the PCIe data path. This feature will enhance confidential VM performance by eliminating the need for a “bounce buffer” when sensitive data within the trust boundary of the confidential VM is shared outside of that trust boundary. This feature will deliver faster data movement, reduce CPU overhead, and improve confidential VM performance without compromising security. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Copilot observability agent
items.description:
Cloud operations need more than reactive troubleshooting, they demand intelligent observability that scales across resources and delivers actionable insights when services aren’t performing as expected.

Introducing the Azure Copilot observability agent that brings a streamlined experience powered by AI-driven investigations, deeper visibility, and faster resolution.

Why It Matters:
  • Smarter insights, faster recovery across your Azure stack
  • Automatic anomaly detection from metrics, logs, and observability signals
  • Correlated findings with clear next steps in natural language
  • Integrated experience with alerts, Azure portal, and Azure Copilot (preview)

Expanded Capabilities:
  • The agent now investigates issues across any Azure resource, including Application Insights (AI), Virtual Machines (VM) and Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
  • Metric analysis for CPU, memory, and network patterns
  • Resource health checks and diagnostics integration for quick remediation
  • Log-enriched anomaly detection for precise root cause identification

What’s New:
  • Extended regional availability – now supported in most Azure regions
  • Copilot support – interact naturally with alerts and dive into investigations with one click

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Online container copy in Azure Cosmos DB
items.description:
You can now minimize downtime when you copy data across containers in Azure Cosmos DB accounts. You can use online container copy in Azure Cosmos DB to copy data from one container to another in real time. Your application using the source container remains online while the data is being copied to the destination container in real time. After your data is completely copied, you can switch over to the new container.  


Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Custom error pages on Azure App Service
items.description:
Custom error pages are now generally available on App Service. When using custom error pages you can configure your apps to present an error page of your choosing instead of the default error pages that are presented to your users. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Dynamic threshold for Log search alerts
items.description:
We’re bringing Azure Monitor’s dynamic threshold capabilities to Log search alerts!
Using dynamic thresholds means you don't have to know the right threshold for each Log alert rule - Dynamic thresholds calculate the most appropriate thresholds for you.

Key benefits
Dynamic thresholds apply advanced machine learning and use a set of algorithms and methods to:

  1. Learn the historical behavior of log query results.
  2. Analyze these results over time and identify hourly / daily / weekly seasonal patterns.
  3. Calculate the most appropriate thresholds for log alert rules.
  4. Adapt automatically to changes in data patterns and adjust the threshold accordingly.
  5. At-scale monitoring - in rule monitoring multiple dimensions - the Dynamic threshold is calculated individually, per dimension combination.
Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Copilot brings new intelligent agents to support end-to-end lifecycle management of workloads
items.description:
Azure Copilot introduces specialized agents (gated preview) to help migrate, operate, and modernize workloads anywhere. Copilot evolves chat into an immersive, full-screen command center (public preview) powered by GPT-5 reasoning, artifact generation, and ARM-driven scenarios. Customers get contextual, multi-modal, and personalized experiences, including chat history and inline actions. A compliance-first architecture and Bring Your Own Storage (public preview) let customers manage chat data securely and control data residency. The new agents (gated preview) are as follows:

  • Deployment Agent: Streamlines environment planning and guided infrastructure deployment.
  • Migration Agent: Automates cloud migration, generates AI recommendations, and modernizes apps.
  • Optimization Agent: Finds cost and carbon savings and enables direct action.
  • Observability Agent: Diagnoses full-stack app issues and suggests mitigation using Azure Monitor.
  • Resiliency Agent: Offers resiliency insights, auto-remediation, and ransomware protection.
  • Troubleshooting Agent: Pinpoints issues, suggests fixes, and guides AKS troubleshooting.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Monitor unified onboarding experience for AKS and VMs
items.description:
Azure Monitor now offers a unified, single-click onboarding experience for both Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) clusters and virtual machines (VMs). This new experience simplifies setup by automatically deploying the latest Azure Monitor capabilities with optimized defaults.

For AKS, the experience combines managed Prometheus metrics, container logs with Kubernetes events, and our newly GAed Dashboards with Grafana. As a part of the new experience, we are also introducing a new application monitoring addon and preconfigured AKS recommended alerts for faster troubleshooting.

For VMs, the onboarding includes new OpenTelemetry-based metrics (now in public preview and free), legacy Log Analytics counters, and recommended VM alerts for comprehensive performance visibility.

This unified experience provides a consistent, streamlined approach to monitoring across your compute environments, helping you get started with Azure Monitor in minutes.

items.title: Public Preview: New AI templates in Microsoft Foundry
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry introduces new ready-to-use, customizable AI templates for popular use cases such as live voice agents, release management, data unification, and SharePoint integration applications. These templates eliminate repetitive setup tasks, reduce deployment friction, and accelerate the journey from concept to production. With customizable code samples, pre-integrated Azure services and GitHub-hosted quick-start guides, development teams can launch faster, customize easily, and scale securely on Microsoft’s trusted AI infrastructure. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Built-in CIS benchmarks for Azure endorsed Linux distros in Machine Config
items.description:
Microsoft Azure now offers built-in Center for Internet Security (CIS) benchmarks in public preview for all Azure endorsed Linux distributions through Azure Machine Configuration’s new customizable security benchmarks capability, powered by azure-osconfig’s compliance engine. This capability allows organizations to easily customize and apply industry-standard security benchmarks which are in parity with the content published on CIS website. It supports both Level 1(L1) and Level 2(L2) server profiles, enables exception and parameter customization, operates in audit-only mode at no additional cost, and extends compliance management to hybrid scenarios via Azure Arc. Using this new capability, you can introduce a flexible, compliance as code driven approach to your organization to maintain security and compliance across your hybrid infrastructure. The solution is officially certified by CIS for CIS benchmark assessment for all the supported benchmarks.  

Learn more:

  • Read our blog and refer to the documentation.  

  • For any questions or feedback fill out this short form.

items.title: Public Preview: Large volumes up to 7.2 PiB
items.description:
The Large Volumes up to 7.2 PiB with Cool Access feature allows you to create Azure NetApp Files volumes up to 7.2 PiB on dedicated capacity, designed for workloads where most data are rarely accessed. This enhancement extends cool-access support beyond the previous 2 PiB limit, giving customers a new scale option for large deployments. By combining petabyte-scale capacity, cool-tier economics, and enterprise-grade performance, organizations can store massive datasets cost-effectively without compromising efficiency. 

This capability helps reduce storage costs for infrequently accessed data while maintaining predictable performance for active workloads. It’s ideal for industries managing large archives, backups, and compliance-driven datasets where 80–90% of data can reside in the cool tier. Use cases include archives, media libraries, healthcare imaging, compliance data lakes, AI/ML datasets, EDA projects, and large file shares—delivering multi-petabyte consolidation, transparent tiering, and lower TCO without sacrificing enterprise-grade performance. 

This feature is supported in all regions that support large volumes. 

Learn more: 

  • What’s New in Azure NetApp Files 

  • Create an SMB volume for Azure NetApp Files 

  • Create an NFS volume for Azure NetApp Files 

  • Create a dual-protocol volume for Azure NetApp Files 

  • Resource limits for Azure NetApp Files

items.title: Public Preview: OpenTelemetry visualizations and enhanced monitoring experience in Azure Monitor for Azure VMs and Arc Servers
items.description:
OpenTelemetry based visualizations in Azure Monitor are in public preview, along with an enhanced, unified monitoring experience for Azure Virtual Machines and Arc Servers. This release consolidates key monitoring capabilities into a single view and introduces a simplified onboarding experience, helping customers more efficiently observe, diagnose, and optimize their environments.

Previously, VM insights visualizations were powered by metric data from Log Analytics. Customers now have the option to power these visualizations using OpenTelemetry (OTel) system metrics, offering a more cost-efficient and performant solution. 

With this feature, you can:
  • Optimize costs by migrating from Log Analytics based metrics to OpenTelemetry metrics
  • Improve performance with faster metric query response times

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Agent mitigations and guardrail customization
items.description:
Introducing guardrails for agents in Microsoft Foundry Control Plane. Formerly called content filters, guardrails can now be applied at the agent level rather than only to model deployments. They include existing controls to help mitigate prompt injection attacks, harms and risks, and to support groundedness. Our newest risk that can be detected, task adherence, helps keep agents on task, detecting when an agent’s next proposed action starts to drift off task.

A new control model also gives you more flexibility in how to configure guardrails and steer agent behavior. Choose what risk you want to monitor, pick where the system should intervene, and decide what action to take. Intervention points include prompts and outputs, and also now includes tool calls and tool responses. Available actions include annotation or blocking.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: New granular controls for network and integration security in Microsoft Foundry
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry streamlines AI development and management for the enterprise. We're introducing more granular controls for network and integration security and resource management that empower IT admins to deploy AI solutions while meeting enterprise-grade security, compliance, and governance requirements. 

Bring Your Own (BYO) Storage for Speech and Language in Foundry is in public preview. Link your own Azure Storage account to Speech and Language services in Foundry Tools, for complete control over where and how data is stored, including access policies and retention. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Streamline IT governance, security, and cost management experiences with Microsoft Foundry
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry streamlines AI development and management for the enterprise. These features are now generally available, empowering IT admins to deploy AI solutions while meeting enterprise-grade security, compliance, and governance requirement: 

  • Manage Foundry costs with Azure Cost Management: Attribute and track costs at the Foundry resource and model deployment level with tags, set budgets with alerts and auto-pause, and provide developers with visibility into costs at the deployment, agent, and run level for AI apps using Azure Cost Management. 
  • Manage Foundry resources with a unified dashboard in Azure Portal: View and manage all resources, projects, connections, users, quota, and API Management integrations for Foundry from a unified dashboard within Azure Portal. 
  • NSP Support for Foundry and Azure OpenAI: Isolate resources within secure, private boundaries using VNETs and private endpoints. This feature ensures data never traverses public networks, simplifies compliance, and strengthens protection against data exfiltration, making it ideal for regulated industries and sensitive workloads. 
  • BYO Key Vault connection for Foundry resources: Securely store and manage secrets, credentials, and encryption keys using your own vaults to ensure compliance. 

Learn more:
  • Set up Key Vault connections
  • Learn about managing AI solutions

items.title: Announcing: Developer Training tier for low-cost fine-tuning training
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry now has a Developer Training tier, offering ultra-low-cost model training by leveraging spot capacity. It’s designed to match the affordability of Developer tier for hosting but applied to the training phase of fine-tuning workflows.​ This tier is ideal for developers testing multiple model variants, MVPs, and teams with low-throughput workloads, enabling rapid experimentation and affordable iteration before scaling production.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Bring Your Own AI Gateway to Foundry Agent Service
items.description:
The BYO AI Model Gateway feature allows enterprises to connect Foundry-hosted models through any AI gateway services like Azure API Management, Mulesoft, and Kong, to Foundry Agent Service. The Agent Service honors pre/post‑LLM hooks, policy‑based model selection, and multi‑region/multi‑provider load‑balancing with automatic failover, so teams can optimize for latency, cost, compliance, and availability without changing application code. This enables organizations to build agents using their own managed endpoints while maintaining enterprise-grade governance, security, and compliance.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: LLM Speech in Microsoft Foundry
items.description:
LLM Speech in Microsoft Foundry brings advanced large language model capabilities to speech, delivering transcription and translation with unmatched fluency and contextual awareness. With enhanced multilingual support and advanced prompt tuning, this API adapts to diverse business needs and outperforms competitors in key benchmarks, providing enterprise-grade speech intelligence and customization.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Microsoft Foundry one-click deploy channels in Teams, M365 and non-Microsoft
items.description: Microsoft Foundry now enables one-click, no-code publishing of custom agents to Microsoft Teams and Microsoft 365 Copilot. This feature removes the complexity of pro-code deployment, allowing organizations to instantly reach millions of users while maintaining compliance, security, and governance. The streamlined process accelerates adoption and unlocks new enterprise scenarios for AI agents.

items.title: Public Preview: Enterprise MCP enhancements in Foundry Agent Service
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry has enhanced integration to Enterprise MCP to enable secure, authenticated connections to MCP servers, allowing credentials to be passed to MCP servers securely. These updates enable enhanced flexibility, security, and compliance when integrating MCP with Microsoft Foundry.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Observability in Foundry Control Plane
items.description:
Observability in Foundry Control Plane now in public preview for agents with a GA pre-announcement for model evals is a comprehensive suite of capabilities that enable developers to evaluate, monitor, and optimize the quality, performance, and safety of multi-agent AI systems. These capabilities are integrated throughout the agent development lifecycle—spanning both build and operate experiences—empowering teams to deliver production-grade AI with confidence and speed. 

Observability in Foundry Control Plane empowers teams to build and manage reliable agents with integrated evaluations (adhoc, continuous on production traffic and scheduled to detect drift), synthetic datasets, and visual cluster analysis for rapid improvement. It provides actionable insights through customizable dashboards, end-to-end OpenTelemetry based tracing, and model upgrade recommendations to optimize cost and performance. Unified observability across agents offers a single view of cost, performance, and security for agents built on Foundry or third-party platforms. Additionally, AI Red Teaming enables continuous safety testing with automated adversarial simulations to uncover vulnerabilities such as data leaks and jailbreaks, ensuring robust and secure AI deployments. 

Learn more:

  • Observability in Generative AI
  • Read about Foundry Control Plane

items.title: Public Preview: Hosted agents in Foundry Agent Service
items.description:
Hosted agents in Foundry Agent Service make it effortless for teams to move from local experimentation to full-scale production.

Developers can now deploy custom-code agents built with Microsoft Agent Framework, LangGraph, CrewAI, or other open-source frameworks directly into a fully managed runtime—no container images, Kubernetes clusters, or deployment pipelines required.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Multi-agent workflows in Foundry Agent Service
items.description:
Developers can now build robust multi-agent workflows using both a visual designer and code-first API. These workflows provide structured orchestration, context sharing, persistent state, and error recovery for complex enterprise processes. The modular design supports secure data handling, extensibility, and long-term state management, making it ideal for advanced automation and enterprise use cases.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Built-in memory in Foundry Agent Service
items.description:
The new long-term memory in Foundry Agent Service gives developers a robust, scalable foundation for agents that can remember, adapt, and act coherently across sessions and workflows. Integrated directly into the Foundry runtime, memory provides a persistent layer where agents can store and retrieve chat summaries, user preferences, and key task outcomes. It enables more natural, consistent, and personalized agent behavior.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Enrich agents with a unified catalog of prebuilt and custom tools in Microsoft Foundry
items.description:
With these latest updates in public preview, Microsoft Foundry enables developers to enrich agents with real-time business context, multimodal capabilities, and custom business logic through a unified catalog of Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools.​


  • Unified tool discovery: Developers can now find, connect, and manage public or private MCP tools for agents from a single, secure interface in Microsoft Foundry.​
  • Deep business integration: Logic Apps connectors provide access to 1,400+ systems like SAP, Salesforce, and HubSpot as MCP tools, enabling agents to quickly integrate with core business services and act on real-time business data and events.​
  • Pre-built AI tools: New Foundry Tools provide out-of-the-box capabilities for transcription, translation, voice, and intelligent document processing, available as MCP servers for rapid agent development.​
  • Custom extensibility: Through API Management, any API or function can be securely exposed as an MCP tool, enabling developers to reuse existing business logic and further accelerate time to value.


Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Content Understanding in Microsoft Foundry
items.description:
With the general availability of Content Understanding, the service now enables connecting to Foundry models, allowing customers to use Foundry model deployments. Additional key updates include support for VNETs, Managed Identities, Customer Managed Keys (CMK), and expanded region coverage. The release also introduces simplified pricing, new domain analyzers, RAG analyzers, and agent tools. Notably, it emphasizes enhanced confidence scores, grounding, and segmentation and routing capabilities, all designed to improve the precision, security, and scalability of AI-powered content analysis and extraction in enterprise environments.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Foundry Tools (rebrand from Azure AI Services)
items.description:
Foundry Tools (rebranded from Azure AI Services) provide a unified suite of prebuilt, production-ready AI capabilities for audio, video, images, documents, and text. Seamlessly integrated into the Microsoft Foundry platform, these tools empower developers to rapidly build intelligent agents and applications with plug-and-play functionality, robust governance, and enterprise-grade security. The rebranding simplifies user experience and accelerates onboarding for agentic AI development.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Foundry IQ by Azure AI Search
items.description: Foundry IQ, powered by Azure AI Search, is a knowledge system that delivers a smarter way to ground agents in enterprise data. Agents only need to connect to a single knowledge base to access multiple sources, removing the need to manage separate APIs and function calls. Knowledge bases perform knowledge retrieval over supported sources including Microsoft SharePoint, Fabric OneLake, and web. Unlike traditional RAG and vector databases, knowledge bases use an agentic retrieval engine holistically across sources and conversations. It also has broader access to data, because it can connect to data remotely or in a synced index. This enables better response quality out of the box, where single-shot retrieval can fall short. Foundry IQ is enterprise-ready, with Purview governance and Entra-based access control, so developers can build with trust and confidence. Create and manage knowledge bases from the Foundry portal, or directly in Azure AI Search.

items.title: Public Preview: Foundry Local updates
items.description:
Foundry Local now extends its capabilities, supporting the Whisper model and advanced on-device AI for smartphones, tablets, and IoT devices. Whisper model integration delivers robust, privacy-preserving speech and audio processing. The redesigned Foundry Local SDK lets developers quickly create and launch AI-driven applications. It features dynamic hardware accelerator compatibility and built-in chat and audio interfaces, all operating independently without needing outside dependencies.

Learn more.

items.title: Private Preview: Foundry Local Android support
items.description:
Foundry Local now extends its capabilities to Android, in addition to Windows and Mac supporting advanced on-device AI for smartphones, tablets, and IoT devices, while Whisper model integration delivers robust, privacy-preserving speech and audio processing. The redesigned Foundry Local SDK lets developers quickly create and launch AI-driven applications. It features dynamic hardware accelerator compatibility and built-in chat and audio interfaces, all operating independently without needing outside dependencies.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Model Router in Microsoft Foundry
items.description:
Model router in Microsoft Foundry is now generally available. Model router is an AI orchestration layer dynamically selects the optimal model for each prompt. It now supports a broader range of models including: GPT-4 family, GPT-5 family, GPT-oss, Deepseek-v3.1, Llama-4-maverick-instruct, Grok-4, and Grok-4-fast. New customization modes – cost savings, quality, and balanced-- allow developers to fine -tune routing logic to best suit their unique needs.  

Additionally, the model router will be added to Foundry Agent Service providing a single, intelligent endpoint that dynamically routes requests to the most suitable model based on task complexity, performance, and cost. This feature simplifies integration, optimizes outcomes, and delivers enterprise resilience to enhance Foundry’s capabilities in multi-model orchestration. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: GitHub Copilot app modernization expanded capabilities
items.description:
Announcing new enhancements to GitHub Copilot App Modernization that are Generally Available, making it easier than ever to modernize applications, databases, containers, and accelerate migration to Azure. Below capabilities are now Generally Available: 

For Java applications:  

  • Improved custom tasks now offer support for diffs, text, and markdown files, along with instructions designed to address specific modernization requirements 
  • Extended IDE support from Visual Studio Code to IntelliJ  

For .NET applications:  

  • Upgrade capabilities to cover .NET Framework to .NET version upgrades for web apps available in Visual Studio  

Containerization capability with containerization assist integration  

  • Automatically generate Dockerfiles and related artifacts such as building images for deployment to Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), AKS Automatic, or Azure Container Apps (ACA)

Deployment on Azure for streamlined modernization and migration:

  • Automatically generate Bicep files and related artifacts for deployment to App Service, App Service Managed Instance, AKS, AKS Automatic, or ACA

These capabilities help streamline modernization projects, reduce manual effort, and accelerate your journey to Azure.

Learn more:

  • Read the blog.
  • Start using GitHub Copilot app modernization.
  • Refer to the Public Preview capabilities at Ignite.

items.title: Public Preview: Microsoft Foundry Control Plane & Entra Agent ID
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry introduces a unified platform for enterprise AI agent observability, security, and governance. The Control Plane integrates identity, monitoring, and compliance, providing centralized control, deep observability, and compliance for agent fleets. Entra Agent ID anchors unified discovery and governance, ensuring agents adhere to enterprise security and Zero Trust standards.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Microsoft Foundry Fine-Tuning Updates
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry Fine-Tuning is updated to reflect a complete redesign of Foundry’s UI, delivering an agent-first experience for developers and data scientists. The new interface streamlines model creation, evaluation, and deployment, integrates with VS Code, and modernizes navigation. With unified workflows and enhanced usability, enterprises can accelerate AI development, reduce friction, and future-proof their agent ecosystem. Public preview launches with full migration planned after July 2025. As a part of this update, Microsoft Foundry now supports Reinforcement Fine-Tuning (RFT) for GPT-5, enabling developers to adapt large language models for specialized, context-aware applications. This update empowers teams to optimize model performance for unique business scenarios, driving innovation and improved outcomes. 

Microsoft Foundry now additionally supports fine-tuning for non-OpenAI models like Mistral using the same APIs, UI, and workflows as GPT-4.1. Developers can fine-tune, deploy, and manage models with full parity across training and deployment, benefiting from quota management and developer tier hosting. This unified experience lowers costs, accelerates iteration, and simplifies production deployment for custom AI solutions. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: OpenShift Virtualization now available on Azure Red Hat OpenShift
items.description:
Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization is now generally available on Azure Red Hat OpenShift (ARO), enabling customers to manage virtual machines and containers from one cloud-native platform. This GA builds on feedback from the preview announced at Red Hat Summit and helps organizations modernize while preserving mission-critical workloads. It simplifies operations with integrated migration tools, Kubernetes-native automation, and cost optimization under consistent governance.

The release adds support for Red Hat Migration Toolkit for Virtualization (MTV), integration with Ansible Automation Platform, and licensing benefits such as included RHEL entitlements and Windows Server licensing through Azure Hybrid Benefit. Organizations can move legacy apps to Azure with minimal disruption, leveraging Azure’s security, compliance, and hybrid features through the OpenShift console. Unifying VMs and containers helps teams speed delivery, apply DevOps practices, and reduce overhead.

Learn more.

FAQ:
Q: Can I migrate existing virtual machines to ARO?
A: Yes, use Red Hat MTV to automate and minimize downtime.
Q: Can I run containers and VMs together?
A: Yes, in a single OpenShift cluster.
Q: What storage is recommended?
A: Use OpenShift Data Foundation; Azure NetApp Files is in preview.
Q: How are support and compliance handled?
A: All ARO clusters receive joint Red Hat–Microsoft support with unified security.

items.title: Generally Available: Premium v2 tier in Azure API Management
items.description:
Announcing the general availability of the Azure API Management Premium v2 tier, our most powerful and scalable option for managing APIs at enterprise scale. 

Premium v2 delivers superior performance, the highest entity limits, unlimited included API calls, and the most comprehensive feature set across all tiers. Designed for large, business-critical API programs, it provides the scale, reliability, and security needed to run enterprise-wide API initiatives with confidence. 

Built on a modernized architecture, Premium v2 separates management traffic from the customer’s virtual network, making private networking both more secure and simpler to configure. 

Learn more:
  • About this high-performance API management tier.
  • Explore pricing details.

items.title: Announcing: API Center Standard now included at no additional cost for linked Azure API Management Standard and Premium tiers
items.description:
API Center Standard, previously a separate paid offering, is now included at no additional cost for all Azure API Management Standard and Premium customers, when an API Center instance is linked with a corresponding Azure API Management service (for both classic and v2 SKUs). 

With this update, organizations can now use API Center Standard without incurring additional charges once integration is configured, bringing even greater value to existing Azure API Management deployments. 

API Center enables teams to track and manage APIs in a centralized location, making it easier to drive discovery, reuse, and governance across the organization. It provides a single source of truth for all APIs, helping teams catalog APIs across environments, improve visibility across the API landscape, and empower developers to find and reuse APIs across teams and business units. 

This update enhances the overall value of Azure API Management, helping customers simplify API operations and accelerate innovation without adding cost or complexity once integration is enabled.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Govern Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoints using Azure API Management
items.description:
Model Context Protocol (MCP) governance in Azure API Management (APIM) is now generally available.

This release extends Azure API Management’s proven governance, security, and observability model to a new generation of AI-driven workloads. Enterprises can now apply consistent policies, authentication, and monitoring across both traditional APIs and AI systems that connect through MCP. 

What’s New:

  • Expose APIs through MCP: Publish any managed API as an MCP-compliant endpoint so AI agents can securely discover and invoke enterprise capabilities using standard protocols. 
  • Proxy and govern external MCP services: Apply Azure API Management policies, authentication, and observability to third-party MCP servers—such as those hosted on Azure Functions, Container Apps etc. or externally hosted MCP servers. 
  • Unify access and governance: Use the same products, policies, and subscription model to manage both API and MCP traffic, ensuring consistent control and visibility across your organization. 
  • Discover and govern through API Center: Register MCP endpoints in Azure API Center to build a private catalog of enterprise MCP integrations, making them easy to discover, onboard, and reuse across teams while maintaining centralized governance and compliance. 

Available across Azure API Management classic and v2 tiers, including the Developer tier and the Self-hosted Gateway. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Automated Testing Framework for Logic Apps [Standard]
items.description:
We’re pleased to announce the general availability of automated testing for Azure Logic Apps (Standard) in the Visual Studio Code extension. This new capability empowers developers and integration specialists to build more reliable workflows by simplifying the unit testing experience directly within their local development environment. 

Starting with version 5.58.8 of the Azure Logic Apps (Standard) extension for Visual Studio Code, you can now: 

  • Generate unit tests from existing workflow runs or saved workflow definitions. 
  • Edit and customize tests directly within Visual Studio Code. 
  • Execute tests locally, enabling faster validation and iteration before deploying to production. 

The enhanced testing experience combines a visual designer interface and an SDK for test script implementation, both powered by the same Test Runner engine to ensure consistency and accuracy of results regardless of the testing approach used. 

You can also execute tests as part of a build or CI/CD pipeline, improving developer productivity and overall code quality through early detection of errors and regressions. 

To get started, update your Azure Logic Apps (Standard) extension in Visual Studio Code and explore the new “Test” features available.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Agent Loop in Azure Logic Apps [Standard]
items.description:
Announcing the general availability of Agent Loop in Azure Logic Apps (Standard), a breakthrough capability that redefines how organizations design and automate business processes. 

Agent Loop enables you to move beyond traditional workflow automation by bringing agentic intelligence into every process. Instead of simply executing predefined steps, Logic Apps can now create goal-driven, adaptive workflows that reason, decide, and act autonomously based on real-time context. 

With Agent Loop, you can: 

  • Build goal-driven workflows that iteratively refine actions until objectives are met. 
  • Use 1,400+ enterprise connectors to give agents real-time access to business systems and data. 
  • Integrate seamlessly with Azure AI Foundry, enabling flexible model and AI service choices. 
  • Ensure traceable reasoning loops with full auditability for compliance and troubleshooting. 

Agent Loop marks a major step forward in bringing agentic capabilities to enterprise integration, making Logic Apps the foundation for intelligent, adaptive business processes. 

Learn more:
  • About building agentic workflows
  • Get started with Agent Loop in Azure Logic Apps.

items.title: Public Preview: Agent Loop in Azure Logic Apps [Consumption]

With this preview, organizations using the consumption-based Logic Apps SKU can now take advantage of Agent Loop’s flexibility and AI integration without changing their existing hosting model. 

With Agent Loop in Consumption, you can:

This public preview extends the power of Agent Loop, enabling you to combine automation, AI, and integration at scale now across both Standard and Consumption Logic Apps environments. 

Learn more:

items.title: Public Preview: New Agent Loop capabilities in Azure Logic Apps
items.description:
Announcing a new set of capabilities for Agent Loop in Azure Logic Apps, now in public preview. These updates expand how organizations can build, secure, and deploy agentic workflows across their enterprise environments enabling more flexible AI orchestration, governance, and collaboration. 

With these new enhancements, you can: 

  • Use and manage MCP servers and tools: Leverage out-of-the-box Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, bring your own, or even create custom MCP servers with user authentication for on-behalf-of (OBO) scenarios extending agentic workflows with secure, policy-driven access to enterprise APIs and systems. 
  • Enable document-level access control: Strengthen governance as agents leverage knowledge sources like Azure AI Search. Using users’ existing Access Control permissions, agents now have scoped access to documents and data ensuring compliance and data security by design. 
  • Bring your own model:  Integrate any model into your agentic workflows, including locally hosted models or those behind private network boundaries. This flexibility allows organizations to maintain control over their model choices and data privacy requirements. 
  • Deploy agents directly to Microsoft Teams: Publish conversational workflows to Microsoft Teams, allowing users to interact with agents natively within Teams for contextual, conversational experiences.
Learn more:
  • About building agentic workflows.
  • Get started with Agent Loop in Azure Logic Apps.

items.title: Public Preview: Redesigned designer experience for Azure Logic Apps [Standard]
items.description:
Announcing the public preview of the redesigned designer experience for Azure Logic Apps (Standard), a major update that makes building, editing, and managing workflows faster and more intuitive. 

The new designer brings run history and workflow editing closer together, allowing you to iterate and troubleshoot in one unified view. It introduces enhanced run visualization options for easier debugging and removes unnecessary clutter from the design-time experience, helping you focus on what matters most, building and optimizing your workflows. 

A new Notes feature enhances collaboration and documentation by letting you add sticky notes directly to your workflow canvas. You can use notes to document logic, provide context for team members, or leave reminders for future updates all within the designer itself. 

This redesigned experience is currently available as an opt-in preview for Logic Apps (Standard) in the Azure portal, with more improvements planned for future releases. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: New Hybrid Integration Connectors for Azure Logic Apps
items.description:
Announcing new capabilities in Azure Logic Apps that expand hybrid integration through a rich set of connectors. 

The following connectors are now generally available: 

  • Confluent Kafka connector: Connect Logic Apps to Confluent Cloud for event streaming and real-time data processing. 
  • XML – Parse and Compose operations: Easily handle complex XML operations, bridging modern workflows with legacy systems and enabling BizTalk migrations. 
  • Inline Code operations (C#, PowerShell, JavaScript): Execute inline code for advanced logic, data manipulation, and integration flexibility. 
  • RabbitMQ connector: Integrate with RabbitMQ for reliable message queuing across distributed systems. Ideal for on-premises scenarios. 

These enhancements strengthen Azure Logic Apps as the foundation for enterprise-grade, event-driven workflows, bridging on-premises, cloud, and industry-specific systems with ease.

items.title: Public Preview: User and group quota reports in Azure NetApp Files
items.description:
For organizations leveraging individual user and group quotas in Azure NetApp Files to manage capacity on NFS, SMB, and dual-protocol volumes, the user and group quota reporting feature offers clear visibility into key metrics such as quota limits, used capacity, and percentage utilization for each target user and group of a quota rule. Administrators can generate quota usage reports and modify quota rules directly within the Azure portal for any volume with quota rules—removing the previous dependency on host-based tools and the need to mount the volume for reporting. This feature is supported in all regions where Azure NetApp Files is available. 

 

Learn more:

  • Azure NetApp Files What's New  

  • Generate user and group quota reports for Azure NetApp Files volumes

items.title: Public Preview: Industry-leading storage performance Ebsv6 VM series
items.description:
Announcing the public preview of the new Azure Ebsv6 VM series, powered by 5th Generation Intel® Xeon® processors. The Ebsv6 and Ebdsv6 VMs deliver up to and industry leading 800,000 IOPS and 14 GBps of remote disk storage throughput, providing high-performance remote storage bandwidth for demanding workloads. This new generation provides up to 2x higher remote storage performance compared to the previous generation, enabling workload consolidation on fewer VMs.

Key new features and improved VM specs compared to Ebsv5/Ebdsv5 

  • Up to 192 vCPU and 1832 GiB memory 

  • 15-30% improvement in CPU performance  

  • 40% larger local SSD capacity with 3X read IOPS 

  • Azure Boost which enables up to: 

    • 800K IOPS and 14GB/s remote storage throughput with Premium v2 and Ultra Disk support 

    • 15% higher remote storage performance per vCPU with up to 6600 IOPS/vCPU 

    • 10% higher remote storage throughput per vCPU 

    • Up to 200 Gbps VM network bandwidth  

    • Enhanced security through Total Memory Encryption (TME) technology 

The Ebsv6 VM series is optimized for large database workloads such as online transaction processing systems, data warehousing applications, and AI/ML workloads that require sequential streaming.

These VMs will initially be available for Public Preview in the US East region. Please sign up for the public preview through this form.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: GitHub Copilot app modernization expanded capabilities
items.description:
Announcing new enhancements to GitHub Copilot App Modernization that are in Public Preview, making it easier than ever to modernize applications, databases, containers, and accelerate migration to Azure. Below are the new capabilities in public preview.  

For .NET applications:  

  • New App Service Managed Instance as a target for easier migration of legacy Windows .NET apps (Public Preview) 

For Python applications: 

  • For Python, customers can now migrate from semantic kernel to agent framework in Visual Studio Code  

Database Modernization:  

  • Modernize PostgreSQL and SQL databases on Azure using the latest PostgreSQL extension (Public Preview) and the SQL Server modernization remains supported through the existing Azure Database Migration Service for SQL migration 

Portfolio Assessment Integration:

  • Integrated portfolio assessment via GitHub Issues with Dr. Migrate and Azure Migrate, and CAST support coming soon. 

These capabilities help streamline modernization projects, reduce manual effort, and accelerate your journey to Azure.

Learn more:

  • Read the blog.
  • Start using GitHub Copilot app modernization. 
  • Refer to the GitHub Copilot app modernization Generally Available capabilities at Ignite.

items.title: Generally Available: Resale enabled offers through Microsoft Marketplace
items.description:
To help commercial customers maximize their technology innovation with Azure, Microsoft Marketplace is fully embracing the channel-led Marketplace opportunity with the general availability of resale enabled offers.  

Resale enabled offers enable software companies to empower channel partners to sell their Marketplace listings through a repeatable model designed for scale. This helps software companies break through to new markets without adding overhead while channel partners maintain their customer relationships while getting the added value of Marketplace. 
 
Sales of eligible solutions also count toward customers’ Azure consumption commitments, opening the door to larger, more strategic deals funded by pre-committed cloud budgets—creating stickier relationships and fueling growth.   

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Microsoft Marketplace
items.description:
Microsoft Marketplace — your trusted source for cloud solutions, AI apps, and agents — is now globally available following its launch in the United States in September. All traffic from legacy storefronts (Azure Marketplace and AppSource) is now redirected to Marketplace.Microsoft.com
 
Featuring the industry’s largest catalog of AI apps and agents, Marketplace extends the Microsoft Cloud, helping customers accelerate their AI-first transformation with tens of thousands of vetted solutions from our partner ecosystem. These solutions integrate easily with Microsoft products, delivering faster time-to-value.

Explore the new Microsoft Marketplace.

items.title: Generally Available: Scheduled Actions
items.description:
Schedule Actions gives the ability to manage the lifecycle of VMs at high scale on a periodic basis. Subscription throttling and retries due to transient errors are handled automatically to ensure that your operations succeed without additional overhead.

What is Scheduled Actions?

Scheduled Actions is a separate resource provider named compute.schedule that sits above our REST API and makes calls on your subscription’s behalf at the time that you specify.

Scheduled Actions supports the following VM operations:

  • Stop
  • Start
  • Hibernate
Why use Scheduled Actions?

  • To schedule power operations on VM resources at scale at up to 5000 concurrent operations.
  • When a higher scale is needed and spreading out call volume is too cumbersome or it's not an option
  • To not have to deal with the complexity of handling throttling issues from the compute stack
  • To offload complexity of determining if the error is transient in nature and needs to be retried. Scheduled Actions handles retries on transient errors.

Learn more:

  • Read the blog.

  • Get started.

items.title: Public Preview: New healthcare connectors for Azure Logic Apps
items.description:
Announcing new capabilities in Azure Logic Apps that expand healthcare interoperability support through a rich set of connectors.

The following connectors are now in public preview:

  • HL7 connector: Enable seamless healthcare data exchange using HL7 messaging standards and BizTalk migrations. 

  • MLLP connector: Provides Minimal Lower Layer Protocol support for integration with healthcare systems, and BizTalk migrations, available in the Logic Apps Hybrid deployment model. 

These enhancements strengthen Azure Logic Apps as the foundation for enterprise-grade, event-driven, and healthcare-integrated workflows, bridging on-premises, cloud, and industry-specific systems with ease.

items.title: Private Preview: ActiveMQ and JMS connector for Azure Logic Apps
items.description: Announcing private preview of Active MQ/JMS connector in Azure Logic Apps. With this capability, you can now connect to enterprise messaging systems built on ActiveMQ and JMS for advanced hybrid integration scenarios.

items.title: Public preview: Support for large volume breakthrough mode
items.description:
Breakthrough mode in Azure NetApp Files enables extreme performance and scalability for demanding HPC and EDA workloads. It supports large volumes up to 2PiB, delivering throughput up to 50GiBps, depending on workload characteristics. Breakthrough mode uses six storage endpoints for each large volume ensuring consistent performance. Storage systems hosting breakthrough mode volumes are reserved for each customer to provide peak performance and not compete with other workloads. 

Key benefits include: 

  • High-capacity scaling for large-scale, latency-sensitive workloads 

  • Simplified network management with multiple storage endpoints per volume 

  • Dedicated capacity stamps to eliminate noisy neighbor interference and maintain predictable performance 

Supported in all regions where large volumes are supported.

 

How to create a volume with large volume breakthrough mode enabled.  

  • Create an NFS volume 

  • Create an SMB volume 

  • Create a dual protocol volume

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: The Archive access tier for Azure Blob Storage is now generally available in the Taiwan North region
items.description:
The Archive access tier for Azure Blob Storage is now generally available in the Taiwan North region.

With this regional expansion, customers in Taiwan can now store infrequently accessed data in the cost-effective Archive tier, while meeting data residency and compliance requirements locally. The Archive tier is ideal for long-term backup, compliance, and archival scenarios, offering the lowest-priced storage option in Azure.

You can manage Archive tier data using the Azure portal, CLI, PowerShell, or REST API. This update brings Taiwan North in line with other regions that support the full range of Azure Blob Storage tiers: Hot, Cool, Cold, and Archive.

items.title: Public Preview: Threat Detection in Azure Backup powered by MDC
items.description:
Azure Backup has introduced threat detection capabilities for Azure VM backups, powered by Microsoft Defender for Cloud (MDC). This new capability enables customers to assess the health of their Azure VM backup restore points (RPs) by identifying malicious or ransomware-infected backups.
By leveraging signals from Microsoft Defender for Servers, Azure Backup detects indicators of compromise such as disruption patterns, heuristic behavior anomalies, and malware or ransomware signatures. This feature is now in public preview in limited regions.

items.title: Public Preview: Query-based metric alerts in Azure Monitor
items.description:
Azure Monitor metric alerts now support all Azure metrics - including platform, Prometheus, and custom metrics - giving you complete coverage for your monitoring needs. 

In addition, metric alerts now offer powerful query capabilities with PromQL, the industry-standard query language, on Prometheus metrics, OTel-based VM performance counters, and other OTel custom metrics ingested into Azure Monitor Workspace (AMW). 

Key Capabilities:

  • PromQL-based conditions: Leverage the full power of PromQL for sophisticated metric selection, aggregation, and transformation. 
  • Flexible scoping: Choose between resource-centric alerts for granular RBAC or workspace-centric alerts for cross-resource visibility. 
  • Managed Identity support: Securely authorize queries using Azure Managed Identity. 
  • Customizable notifications: Add dynamic custom properties and custom email subjects for faster triage and context-rich alerting. 

With query-based metric alerts, you can detect complex patterns, reduce alert noise, and reuse existing community-based Prometheus alert logic - all while maintaining a unified monitoring experience in Azure. This feature empowers teams to proactively manage performance and reliability at scale, without sacrificing flexibility or security.

items.title: Public Preview: Introducing SDK Stats to the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Distro
items.description:
As part of our journey to make Azure the most observable cloud, we are adding a new way for you to observe your Azure Monitor Application Insights data collection pipeline. 

One of the foremost reasons customers file support tickets against Azure Monitor Application Insights is that they are not seeing the data they expect.

Now, you can leverage the built-in SDK Stats workbook to quickly spot and resolve ingestion issues, ensuring your apps stay observable and reliable.

SDK Stats emits new per-process metrics that track successful sends, drops, and retries—complete with detailed reason codes. To get this powerful, new capability, upgrade to the latest version of the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Distro.

Learn More.

items.title: Generally Available: Visual Studio 2026
items.description:
Visual Studio 2026 is the next evolution of the world’s most trusted IDE—modernized with AI deeply integrated into everyday workflows. By seamlessly integrating GitHub Copilot and agentic workflows, Visual Studio empowers professional developers to move faster, reduce toil, and deliver higher-quality software. Combined with modern UX, blazing performance, and enterprise-grade trust, Visual Studio remains the IDE of choice for complex, mission-critical development. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Capacity guidance for Azure Site Recovery
items.description:
Azure Site Recovery now offers alternative VM Size recommendations during ASR failover when the current target VM Size may have limited allocation availability due to capacity constraints. This feature enhances disaster recovery by providing guidance on suitable VM size alternatives, thereby increasing the likelihood of successful VM allocation during failover events. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Support 5x churn in Azure Site Recovery
items.description:
Azure Site Recovery now supports up to 5x churn (500 MB/s per VM). This major enhancement empowers customers to confidently run high IOPS workloads with Azure Site Recovery, ensuring robust disaster recovery for even the most demanding applications like databases, big data and analytics systems, etc. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Support for Linux major OS upgrades with Azure Site Recovery
items.description:
You can now perform major Linux OS version upgrades — without disabling Azure Site Recovery, interrupting their replication, or losing existing recovery points. This is supported on RHEL and SLES. (e.g. update from RHEL 8 to RHEL 9). This simplifies the OS upgrade lifecycle and eliminates downtime in disaster recovery posture. This feature is currently available for Azure-to-Azure (A2A) disaster recovery scenario.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Seamless failback for HyperV-to-Azure: Managed Disk support in Azure Site Recovery
items.description:
Azure Site Recovery now enables failback from Azure VMs to on-premises Hyper-V, even if replication from on-premises to Azure happened to storage account and the failed-over Azure VM uses managed disks. 

Learn more.

items.title: Retirement: Support for Python 3.10 ends on October 1st, 2026
items.description:
On October 1, 2026 extended support for Python 3.10 will end. Your apps that are hosted on App Service will continue to run, but security updates will no longer be available, and we’ll no longer provide customer service for Python 3.10. Learn more about App Service language support. 

Required action 

To avoid potential security vulnerabilities and minimize risk for your App Service apps, follow the steps to upgrade your app to Python 3.11 before October 1, 2026.

items.title: Retirement: Windows Server 2022 on Azure Kubernetes Service enabled by Azure Arc
items.description: Announcing the retirement of Windows Server 2022 on Azure Kubernetes Service enabled by Azure Arc in October 2026.

items.title: Public Preview: Pod CIDR expansion in Azure CNI Overlay for AKS
items.description:
Pod CIDR expansion in Azure CNI Overlay for AKS is now available in public preview. 

To meet the growing demands of dynamic and large-scale Kubernetes workloads, Azure Kubernetes Service now offers Pod CIDR Expansion in public preview for clusters using Azure CNI Overlay. While Azure CNI Overlay already delivers scalable pod IP address management via a logical overlay network, many enterprise customers require additional flexibility to support evolving business needs. 

This new capability allows users to expand existing pod CIDR ranges, enhancing both scalability and adaptability for workloads that require more IP space. The preview currently supports CIDR range expansion only, enabling organizations to better manage IP allocation without redeploying clusters. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: eBPF host routing in Advanced Container Networking Services for AKS
items.description:
eBPF host routing in Advanced Container Networking Services for AKS is now available in public preview. 


As containerized applications scale across distributed environments, traditional networking approaches can introduce latency and reduce throughput. To address this, Azure CNI powered by Cilium now offers eBPF Host Routing in public preview for Azure Kubernetes Service. 

This feature uses eBPF technology to embed routing logic directly into the Linux kernel, eliminating the need for iptables and reducing reliance on the host network stack. By enabling Cilium to make direct routing decisions, eBPF host routing delivers lower latency, fewer network hops, and higher throughput for Kubernetes clusters. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Virtual Network Manager UseExisting Mode for UDR management
items.description:
Azure Virtual Network Manager UDR management now offers UseExisting mode, providing customers with greater flexibility and compliance control over user-defined routes (UDRs). 

With the UseExisting mode, Azure Virtual Network Manager detects and appends required routes to an existing route table associated with a subnet, preserving the original route table’s name, group, and tags. If no route table exists, Azure Virtual Network Manager automatically creates one as before. Customers seeking Azure Virtual Network Manager-managed route tables can continue using the existing Managed Only mode (the default). 

This general availability release empowers customers to: 

  • Maintain governance compliance by retaining ownership of route table configurations 
  • Simplify operations with seamless integration of AVNM automation into existing environments 
  • Enhance flexibility by choosing how AVNM interacts with routing resources  

The UseExisting mode makes it easier than ever to adopt Azure Virtual Network Manager UDR management at scale—combining centralized automation with customer-driven governance and control. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Virtual Network Manager peering compliance
items.description:
Azure Virtual Network Manager peering compliance is now generally available, providing a secure and compliant mechanism to protect network connectivity managed by Azure Virtual Network Manager. 

In large-scale environments, it’s essential to prevent unintentional changes to critical connectivity configurations. With peering compliance, any virtual network peering created and managed through Azure Virtual Network Manager topology is safeguarded from accidental modification or deletion by virtual network owners outside of Azure Virtual Network Manager. 

This release allows users to enforce compliance by restricting direct edits to key peering properties and preventing deletion of peerings. Changes can only be made through Azure Virtual Network Manager connectivity configurations, ensuring consistency and governance across your environment.  

With this general availability release, customers gain stronger governance controls, reduced configuration drift, and higher confidence that network topologies remain secure and compliant across teams and subscriptions. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Virtual Network Manager IP Address Management Pool Association Recommendation
items.description:
Azure Virtual Network Manager IP Address Management (IPAM) – Pool Association Recommendation is now generally available, bringing intelligent, large-scale automation to IP address management in Azure. 

As organizations expand their network footprint across regions and management groups, identifying and associating virtual networks with the right IPAM pools can become increasingly complex. Unassociated virtual networks may consume overlapping address spaces, raising the risk of conflicts during provisioning. 

With Pool Association Recommendation, customers can now automatically identify all virtual networks within their Network Manager scope that are not yet associated with an IPAM pool. The feature intelligently recommends the most suitable pool for each virtual network by applying longest-prefix matching within the pool hierarchy, ensuring optimal fit and capacity alignment. 

Administrators can bulk select and associate virtual networks in a single action directly from the Azure portal—streamlining operations, reducing manual effort, and ensuring full coverage at scale. 

This general availability release empowers customers to manage address spaces more efficiently, minimize configuration drift, and maintain consistent governance across large, distributed Azure environments. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: .NET 10
items.description: .NET 10 delivers a faster, more secure, and more capable platform for modern development. This release enhances performance, productivity, and security across the stack—while C# 14 introduces refinements that make coding more natural and expressive. With smarter tooling and a streamlined developer experience, .NET 10 helps teams build intelligent, reliable, and scalable applications with greater speed and confidence.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Database for MySQL Triggers for Azure Functions
items.description:
Azure Database for MySQL triggers for Azure Functions are now generally available, enabling you to set up change tracking and develop event-driven applications at scale on any MySQL table. You can trigger a function when a row in a MySQL table is created, updated, or deleted.   

 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Scheduler profile configuration for AKS
items.description:
Organizations running complex workloads on Kubernetes often face challenges in optimizing pod placement for performance, cost, or resource efficiency. To address this, Azure Kubernetes Service now offers scheduler profile configuration with in-tree plugins, available in public preview. This new capability enables users to customize scheduling behavior and define workload priorities across specific nodes or the entire cluster. It’s especially beneficial for advanced scenarios such as data processing, AI/ML, and cost-optimized workload distribution. 

Learn more.

items.title: General Availability: Server Parameters support for lower_case_table_names in Azure Database for MySQL- Flexible Server
items.description:
We are thrilled to announce the General Availability of a highly requested feature: Self-serve configuration of the lower_case_table_names server parameter during server creation. For MySQL version 8.0+ you can configure lower_case_table_names only when you're initializing the server. For restore operations or replica server creation, the parameter will automatically be copied from the source server and cannot be changed.  

 

Learn more

items.title: Generally Available: LocalDNS for AKS
items.description:
LocalDNS for AKS is now generally available.  

 

Large-scale Kubernetes clusters often face DNS resolution delays and reliability issues, especially during upstream outages or high query volumes. To address this, Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) now offers LocalDNS, a feature that is generally available. 

LocalDNS deploys a DNS proxy on each node, enabling faster and more reliable DNS resolution by handling queries locally. This eliminates bottlenecks, reduces latency, and ensures continued resolution even during upstream DNS outages through configurable serve-stale settings. 

With no application-level changes required, LocalDNS delivers immediate performance improvements and supports advanced DNS customization for both internal and external domains. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Insights in Azure Migrate
items.description:
Azure Migrate now offers integrated Security insights, allowing customers to assess potential risks within their on-premises environment. The solution delivers actionable recommendations to effectively mitigate these risks as part of the migration planning. It uses improved Software inventory to identify use of multiple security tools and suggests consolidation with Microsoft Defender for Cloud. Notable aspects of the solution:
  1. Review security risks in your datacenter early during migration planning.
  2. Plan mitigation to fix security issues and make your migration to Azure smooth and secure.
  3. Identify and plan upgrade of Windows and Linux servers with end of support operating system, end of support software and pending updates.
  4. Review and plan upgrade of databases running on end of support databases platform and web apps built on end of support runtime. 
  5. Detect vulnerabilities in servers, databases, web apps and discovered software and take action to remediate risks.
  6. Identify servers without security or patch management software, and plan to configure Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Azure Update Manager.
Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Vaulted Backup for Azure Data Lake Storage (ADLS)
items.description:
Azure Backup vaulted protection for ADLS Gen2 delivers secure, off‑site backups to help organizations meet resilience and compliance goals. Vaulted backups maintain an independent copy of your data, isolated from the source account - providing protection against accidental deletion, malicious activity, and ransomware. 

 

Capabilities at a Glance: 

  • Off‑site protection: Recover data safely by restoring to alternate storage accounts to support clean recovery workflows. 
  • Automated & flexible scheduling: Configure daily or weekly backup policies and trigger on‑demand backups when needed. 
  • Long‑term retention: Store backups for up to 10 years to meet compliance and archival requirements. 
  • Security‑first design: Soft‑delete, immutability, encryption, and multi‑user authorization protect backup data in the vault. 

Scope and availability at GA: 
Vaulted backups can be configured for block blobs in Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 accounts. General availability will start with a subset of the regions from Public Preview list. We will continue expanding to additional regions over the coming months. 

Learn more:
  • Configure Vaulted Backup for ADLS
  • Support matrix & limits
  • Pricing

items.title: Generally Available: Azure WAF JavaScript challenge on Azure Front Door
items.description:
Announcing the general availability of JavaScript (JS) challenge for Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) with Azure Front Door 

To strengthen bot mitigation strategies, Azure WAF now introduces JS challenge as a new security feature. The JS challenge provides an invisible, frictionless layer of protection by distinguishing legitimate users from malicious bots without requiring human interaction. Unlike CAPTCHA, this challenge runs silently in the background, reducing user disruption while effectively blocking harmful automated traffic. 

Key benefits include: 

  • Enhanced bot protection: Malicious bots fail the JS challenge, safeguarding your applications. 
  • Improved user experience: Legitimate users are not interrupted, ensuring seamless access. 
  • Flexible integration: Available as a mitigation action in the Bot Managed ruleset and custom rules. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Agentic CLI for AKS
items.description:
Diagnosing and resolving issues in Kubernetes clusters can be complex and time-consuming, especially when navigating logs, telemetry, and diagnostics manually. To simplify this experience, Azure Kubernetes Service is introducing a new agentic AI-powered CLI experience through the “az aks agent” command. 

This new capability brings agentic reasoning directly into the Azure CLI, allowing developers and operators to interact with their clusters using natural language. By describing an issue or query, users can trigger an intelligent agentic loop that gathers signals from multiple sources, analyzes diagnostics, identifies health issues and root causes, and provides actionable recommendations. The CLI agent also integrates with the AKS MCP server and can seamlessly create and manage an Azure OpenAI instance, though it supports any LLM provider. 

Powered by HolmesGPT - an open-source project co-maintained by the AKS team and accepted as a CNCF sandbox project- this feature is now available in public preview. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Flatcar Container Linux for AKS
items.description:
Maintaining consistent and secure node configurations in Kubernetes environments can be challenging due to issues like configuration drift, manual changes, and complex upgrade paths. These challenges often lead to unpredictable behavior and increased operational overhead. 

Azure Kubernetes Service now supports Flatcar Container Linux in public preview. Flatcar is built on an immutable filesystem, which helps ensure predictable node behavior by preventing unauthorized changes and simplifying recovery from security incidents. As a Cloud Native Compute Foundation (CNCF) project, Flatcar also supports cross-cloud deployment, making it a strong choice for organizations seeking enhanced security and operational efficiency across diverse environments. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Linux OS Guard for AKS
items.description:
Cloud-native workloads face increasingly sophisticated threats—from rootkits and container escapes to unauthorized code execution—that demand stronger security guarantees. To address these challenges, Microsoft has introduced Azure Linux with OS Guard, now available in public preview. 

Built on the FedRAMP-certified Azure Linux 3.0 base, OS Guard is a next-generation immutable container host that enforces immutability, code integrity, and mandatory access control. It leverages advanced technologies like dm-verity, SELinux, and Integrity Policy Enforcement (IPE)—recently upstreamed in Linux kernel 6.12—to ensure only trusted binaries from signed sources can run, while locking down user space against tampering. With Trusted Launch enabled by default, OS Guard also secures boot components using measured integrity backed by vTPM keys. 

Azure Linux is the trusted OS powering Microsoft’s own fleet, and OS Guard builds on that foundation to deliver enhanced protection for cloud-native environments. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: DNS flow trace logs for Azure Firewall
items.description:
Azure Firewall now supports DNS flow trace logs — a new logging capability that gives you deep, end-to-end visibility into DNS traffic and name resolution paths. This enhancement provides richer telemetry to help you troubleshoot, validate, and secure DNS flows across your network. 

DNS flow trace logs build on existing DNS Proxy functionality by logging critical metadata including query types, response codes, queried domains, upstream DNS servers, and the source and destination IPs of each request. These insights enable faster diagnosis of application connectivity issues, improved auditing, and better security investigations. 

Key highlights                                                                  

  • End-to-end DNS visibility — see each step of DNS resolution across your environment 
  • Faster troubleshooting — pinpoint DNS failures and validate forwarding and custom DNS configuration 
  • Cache insights  -- determine whether the Azure Firewall cache was used for DNS resolution 
Learn more:
  • Read the monitoring data reference documentation.
  • Learn about Azure Firewall Prescaling.

items.title: Generally Available: Geo Priority Replication for Azure Blob
items.description:
Geo priority replication enhances the replication process for GRS and GZRS storage accounts by enabling accelerated data replication between the primary and secondary regions. This feature is backed by a Service Level Agreement (SLA), ensuring the Last Sync Time for Block Blob data remains at 15 minutes or less, 99.0% of the billing month. With this guaranteed sync time, users can feel more confident about their data’s durability and availability, especially if an unexpected outage occurs in their primary region and a failover is required. 


Geo Priority Replication applies to Block Blob.  

Learn more.
